@bettervoxel/global/BrickColor.documentation: The BrickColor constructors — see the BrickColor page.

@bettervoxel/global/BrickColor.Random.documentation: random under its other spelling: the same draw.

@bettervoxel/global/BrickColor.new.documentation: Really black (1003) with no argument; a number, truncated toward zero — 194 when the table has none; a name, case-sensitive — 194 for an unknown one, a numeric string read as a number; three channels 0..1 (a missing one 0) or a Color3, the nearest colour by the least sum of absolute channel differences (the first in number order on a tie; nothing clamped).

@bettervoxel/global/BrickColor.palette.documentation: The 128-entry palette's colour at a zero-based index, rounded to the nearest (a half away from zero); out of bounds raises `palette index out of bounds (<index>)`.

@bettervoxel/global/BrickColor.random.documentation: A colour of the 128-entry palette, drawn from the VM's own generator — the stream math.random draws, so a session replayed under a seed replays it.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.documentation: The CFrame constructors — see the CFrame page.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.Angles.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame from XYZ Euler angles in radians — the canonical spelling of fromEulerAnglesXYZ (measured: the X·Y·Z product, matching the reference).

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromAxisAngle.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame around axis (a nonzero vector) by angle radians.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromEulerAngl.documentation: A rotation-only CFrame from Euler angles in radians: the product of the three axis rotations in the order's letters, left to right (an Enum.RotationOrder item, XYZ by default), the angles always rx, ry, rz.
A rotation-only CFrame from XYZ Euler angles in radians — the same axis order the instance Rotation property uses (in degrees there).
A rotation-only CFrame from YXZ Euler angles in radians: the product Ry·Rx·Rz, the angles still passed as rx, ry, rz (measured).

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromMatrix.documentation: A CFrame at pos from a rotation matrix's columns, orthonormalized: Gram–Schmidt over vX then vY, the third column their cross — a CFrame here is a rotation, so vZ is taken and not kept (the reference keeps all three columns as given).

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromOrientati.documentation: fromEulerAnglesYXZ under its other name: the Ry·Rx·Rz product of rx, ry, rz in radians.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.fromRotationB.documentation: The shortest rotation taking the direction of from onto that of to; opposite directions take a half turn about from × Y when |from.X| > |from.Y|, else about from × X; a zero vector is an all-NaN rotation.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.identity.documentation: The identity transform: zero position, no rotation.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.lookAlong.documentation: A CFrame at position with its LookVector along direction — lookAt aimed at position + direction, by the same rule for the up.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.lookAt.documentation: A CFrame at position with its LookVector aimed at target; up defaults to the world Y axis, and the X axis stands in for an up parallel to the look.

@bettervoxel/global/CFrame.new.documentation: The identity (no arguments), a translation from a position vector or from x, y, z, the legacy two-vector form (a position looking at a point: Y up, the X axis the up once the look is within about eight degrees of the vertical), a position and a quaternion (normalized; a zero one is an all-NaN rotation), or a position and a rotation matrix row by row (orthonormalized: Gram–Schmidt over the X then the Y column, the third their cross).

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.documentation: The Color3 constructors — see the Color3 page.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.fromHSV.documentation: A color from hue, saturation and value, all 0..1; the hue wraps.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.fromHex.documentation: A color from three or six hex digits in either case after an optional #, the short form's digits doubled; a number is read as its digits.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.fromRGB.documentation: A color from byte components, clamped 0..255 — the editor color picker's scale.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.new.documentation: A color from sRGB components 0..1 (unclamped); omitted components default to 0.

@bettervoxel/global/Color3.toHSV.documentation: Deprecated: the function form of ToHSV — the hue, saturation and value of color, answered as color:ToHSV() (measured) — use ToHSV.

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequence.documentation: The ColorSequence constructors — see the ColorSequence page.

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequence.new.documentation: A constant color, a straight ramp between two colors, or the given keypoints — 2 to 20 of them, the first at time 0, the last at time 1, in time order.

@bettervoxel/global/ColorSequenceKeypoin.documentation: The ColorSequenceKeypoint constructors — see the ColorSequenceKeypoint page.
A keypoint at time (0..1) holding a color.

@bettervoxel/global/Enum.documentation: The enum families; every item is an EnumItem.

@bettervoxel/global/Font.documentation: The Font constructors — see the Font page.

@bettervoxel/global/Font.fromEnum.documentation: The face a legacy Enum.Font item names: the reference's catalog family (`rbxasset://fonts/families/<Family>.json`, rendered as the engine default face at the item's weight and style) — the same face the Font property stores, so fromEnum(label.Font) == label.FontFace after a Font write. Enum.Font.Unknown refuses.

@bettervoxel/global/Font.new.documentation: A Font from a local font asset path — Regular and Normal unless given. Weight and style must be enum items (a name string is refused, as measured).

@bettervoxel/global/Instance.documentation: The Instance constructors — see the Instance page.

@bettervoxel/global/Instance.new.documentation: A default-constructed instance of the named class, with Parent nil — assign Parent to bring it into the world (derived state appears on attach). Only creatable classes are accepted; abstract and engine-spawned classes error exactly like an unknown name.

@bettervoxel/global/Keybinds.documentation: The game's authored keybinds by name: each is a signal that fires with an action on its key's press and on its release — the action's `pressed` is true on the press, its `state` names it ("Pressed" or "Released"). Quiet while a TextBox has the focus.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberRange.documentation: The NumberRange constructors — see the NumberRange page.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberRange.new.documentation: A range from its ends (min must not exceed max), or a single value as both ends.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequence.documentation: The NumberSequence constructors — see the NumberSequence page.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequence.new.documentation: A constant sequence, a straight line between two values, or the given keypoints — 2 to 20 of them, the first at time 0, the last at time 1, in time order.

@bettervoxel/global/NumberSequenceKeypoi.documentation: The NumberSequenceKeypoint constructors — see the NumberSequenceKeypoint page.
A keypoint at time (0..1) with a value and an optional random envelope (default 0).

@bettervoxel/global/Random.documentation: The Random constructors — see the Random page.

@bettervoxel/global/Random.new.documentation: A generator from a seed — truncated toward zero, a negative one its two's complement, a magnitude of 2^53 or more seed 0, NaN the bits of -2^63 (measured) — or, with no seed, from the VM's own generator: the stream math.random draws, so a session replayed under a seed replays it.

@bettervoxel/global/Ray.documentation: The Ray constructors — see the Ray page.

@bettervoxel/global/Ray.new.documentation: A ray from origin along direction (kept at the given length — Unit normalizes it).

@bettervoxel/global/RaycastParams.documentation: The RaycastParams constructors — see the RaycastParams page.

@bettervoxel/global/RaycastParams.new.documentation: The defaults: FilterType Exclude over an empty list, the new pair nil, the flags false, CollisionGroup "Default", ServerTime nil.

@bettervoxel/global/Signals.documentation: Named cross-script channels (BindableEvent-style): every script of the context reaches the same signal by its name, and the payloads are real Lua values — tables, functions and instances pass as they are.

@bettervoxel/global/Signals.Fire.documentation: Fires the channel with the arguments. Delivery is deferred to the next flush, and a name nobody read fires into nothing.

@bettervoxel/global/Signals.Get.documentation: The channel's signal: made on the first read of the name, the same value after — connect to it as to any signal.

@bettervoxel/global/TweenInfo.documentation: The TweenInfo constructors — see the TweenInfo page.

@bettervoxel/global/TweenInfo.new.documentation: Bundles the parameters TweenService:Create consumes. Defaults follow the reference engine: 1 second, Quad, Out, no repeats, no reverse, no delay; time and delay floor at 0.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim.documentation: The UDim constructors — see the UDim page.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim.new.documentation: A UDim from its two components, each 0 when omitted: parent fraction plus pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.documentation: The UDim2 constructors — see the UDim2 page.

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.fromOffset.documentation: A UDim2 with only the pixel offsets set (scales zero).

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.fromScale.documentation: A UDim2 with only the scale components set (offsets zero).

@bettervoxel/global/UDim2.new.documentation: A UDim2 from its four components: per-axis parent fraction plus pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector2.documentation: The Vector2 constructors — see the Vector2 page.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector2.new.documentation: A Vector2 from its components; a missing component is zero.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector3.documentation: The Vector3 constructors — see the Vector3 page.

@bettervoxel/global/Vector3.new.documentation: A vector from its components; omitted components default to 0. The result IS a native Luau vector — Vector3.new(1, 2, 3) equals vector.create(1, 2, 3), and typeof says 'vector' (a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/global/collectgarbage.documentation: Luau's memory reading under the sandbox: `collectgarbage("count")` is the heap's size in kilobytes; every other option is refused.

@bettervoxel/global/debug.documentation: Luau's debug library (`traceback`, `info`) plus the reference's profiler and memory-category extras, which validate their arguments and do nothing else here.

@bettervoxel/global/delay.documentation: The legacy delay: runs the callback after the given seconds (floored at 1/30 s), passing the seconds elapsed and elapsedTime(). Prefer task.delay.

@bettervoxel/global/elapsedTime.documentation: Seconds since this process booted its first script context.

@bettervoxel/global/game.documentation: The DataModel: `game:GetService(name)` hands out the engine services.

@bettervoxel/global/script.documentation: The running script's own instance, a LuaSourceContainer — `script.Parent` navigates from it.

@bettervoxel/global/spawn.documentation: The legacy spawn: runs the callback one legacy cycle (1/30 s) later, never in place, passing the seconds elapsed and elapsedTime(). Prefer task.spawn or task.defer.

@bettervoxel/global/task.documentation: The scheduler library the VM opens: wait, spawn, defer, delay and cancel over the scheduler each step resumes. A function handed to spawn, defer or delay runs on a new thread; a thread handed to them is resumed.

@bettervoxel/global/task.cancel.documentation: Closes the thread as coroutine.close does: a suspended or not yet started thread never runs again (its finalizers run as cancelled); the running thread is refused.

@bettervoxel/global/task.defer.documentation: Runs the function, or resumes the thread, at the end of the current step with the given arguments. Returns the thread.

@bettervoxel/global/task.delay.documentation: Runs the function, or resumes the thread, once the given seconds have passed, with the given arguments. Returns the thread.

@bettervoxel/global/task.desynchronize.documentation: Does nothing: scripts run on one thread of execution here, so there is no parallel phase to switch to.

@bettervoxel/global/task.spawn.documentation: Runs the function, or resumes the thread, at once and in place with the given arguments; an error it raises is reported, never propagated to the caller. Returns the thread.

@bettervoxel/global/task.synchronize.documentation: Does nothing: scripts run on one thread of execution here, so there is no serial phase to switch to.

@bettervoxel/global/task.wait.documentation: Yields the running thread until at least the given seconds have passed — the next step when omitted — and returns the seconds it slept.

@bettervoxel/global/tick.documentation: Seconds since the Unix epoch on this machine's clock, with sub-second precision.

@bettervoxel/global/time.documentation: Seconds the game has been running with scripts live — the pause-aware script clock.

@bettervoxel/global/wait.documentation: The legacy sleep: yields at least the given seconds (floored at 1/30 s, the floor alone with no argument) and returns the seconds slept, then elapsedTime(). Prefer task.wait.

@bettervoxel/global/warn.documentation: Prints its arguments to the output as a warning (an engine global — plain Luau has no `warn`).

@bettervoxel/global/workspace.documentation: The Workspace root — the container every world object lives under.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignOrientation.documentation: A mover: a torque that turns Attachment0 to Attachment1's orientation, or to CFrame's with one attachment — the whole orientation, its primary axis alone, or that axis toward a point (AlignType; LookAtPosition with one attachment) — as quickly as Responsiveness asks and within MaxTorque and MaxAngularVelocity.

Whether the alignment acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body in TwoAttachment mode (measured: OneAttachment needs Attachment0 alone). Read only.

What turns: AllAxes (the default) the whole orientation; PrimaryAxisParallel Attachment0's X parallel to the goal's X; PrimaryAxisLookAt Attachment0's X toward LookAtPosition (one attachment) or Attachment1's position (two). Parallel, Perpendicular and PrimaryAxisPerpendicular are refused (a recorded divergence).
The goal orientation in OneAttachment mode: Attachment0 turns to its rotation; its translation is saved and ignored, as the reference's (a look-at aims at LookAtPosition). Default identity.
The world point Attachment0's X turns toward when AlignType is PrimaryAxisLookAt and Mode is OneAttachment. Neither saved nor replicated: a client's is its own. Default (0, 0, 0).
The speed Attachment0 turns toward its goal at, at most, in radians per second. Default inf.
The most torque the alignment turns with; math.huge is no limit. Default 10000.
TwoAttachment (the default) turns Attachment0 to Attachment1's orientation; OneAttachment turns it to CFrame's.
The goal's X axis in OneAttachment mode — a view of CFrame's rotation: a write turns the goal so its X is the axis, keeping its Y as near as perpendicularity allows. Default (1, 0, 0).
Deprecated on the reference: set AlignType instead. True makes AllAxes turn the primary axes alone, as PrimaryAxisParallel does. Default false.
Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite torque (TwoAttachment mode). Default false.

How quickly Attachment0 turns to its goal: an approach without overshoot that settles in about 13 / Responsiveness seconds (45 is within 1 degree of a quarter turn at 0.32 s, measured). Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end (measured), an infinite one included; a NaN write is refused. Default 10.
Always false: the rigid alignment is not built, and a write of true is refused (a recorded divergence).
The goal's Y axis in OneAttachment mode — a view of CFrame's rotation: a write turns the goal about its X toward the axis. Default (0, 1, 0).
Draws the editor's marker for the alignment whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.documentation: A mover: a force that carries Attachment0 to Attachment1, or to Position with one attachment, as quickly as Responsiveness asks and within MaxForce and MaxVelocity — holding the assembly's weight while it does.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Ac.documentation: Whether the alignment acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body in TwoAttachment mode or when the per-axis limit is in its frame (measured: OneAttachment needs Attachment0 alone). Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Ap.documentation: Whether the force acts at the assembly's centre of mass instead of at Attachment0. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Fo.documentation: Magnitude (the default) holds the force's length to MaxForce; PerAxis holds each axis of ForceRelativeTo's frame to its lane of MaxAxesForce.
The frame whose axes the PerAxis limit applies along: the world's (the default), Attachment0's or Attachment1's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Ma.documentation: The most force along each axis of ForceRelativeTo's frame under the PerAxis limit; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (10000, 10000, 10000).
The most force the alignment pushes with under the Magnitude limit — the assembly's weight included; math.huge is no limit. Default 10000.
The speed Attachment0 approaches its goal at, at most, in studs per second (measured as an exact cap). Default inf.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Mo.documentation: TwoAttachment (the default) carries Attachment0 to Attachment1; OneAttachment carries it to Position.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Po.documentation: The goal in world space in OneAttachment mode: Attachment0 is carried there. Default (0, 0, 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Re.documentation: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite force (TwoAttachment mode). Default false.

How quickly Attachment0 reaches its goal: an approach without overshoot that settles in about 13 / Responsiveness seconds (45 is within 0.1 stud of a 10-stud goal at 0.32 s, measured). Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end (measured), an infinite one included; a NaN write is refused. Default 10.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Ri.documentation: Always false: the rigid alignment is not built, and a write of true is refused (a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AlignPosition.Vi.documentation: Draws the editor's marker for the alignment whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AngularVelocity.documentation: A mover: a torque that brings Attachment0's assembly to an angular velocity within each physics step, named in RelativeTo's frame, within MaxTorque — whose default 0 turns nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/AngularVelocity..documentation: Whether the angular velocity target acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it; the fresh zero MaxTorque leaves it active (measured). Read only.

The angular velocity, radians per second, the torque brings Attachment0's assembly to within each physics step, in RelativeTo's frame — relative to Attachment1's assembly under Attachment1. Default (0, 0, 0).
The most torque the target spins the assembly with; the default 0 turns nothing, as does any value of 0 or less (the hinge's rule); math.huge is no limit.
Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite torque — with RelativeTo Attachment1, the frame it is meaningful in. Default false.
The frame AngularVelocity is named in: the world's (the default), Attachment0's, or Attachment1's — the spin then relative to Attachment1's assembly.
Draws the editor's marker for the angular velocity target whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.documentation: A named point on a part: its CFrame, Position and Orientation are LOCAL to the parent, and the WorldCFrame/WorldPosition pair is the composed world view (writing it recomputes the local). Constraints anchor to attachments; Visible draws the editor marker.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.CFram.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL pose relative to its parent part (§15); the world-space view is WorldCFrame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Orien.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL rotation as YXZ Euler angles in degrees: (rx, ry, rz) names the product Ry·Rx·Rz, where CFrame.Angles composes Rx·Ry·Rz (§30).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Posit.documentation: The attachment's LOCAL position, relative to its parent part (§15). The world-space view is WorldPosition.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.Visib.documentation: Draws the editor's marker gizmo at the attachment's world pose. Purely an authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Attachment.World.documentation: The attachment's world pose: the parent part's pose composed with the local CFrame — the local values when no posed parent exists. Writing it recomputes the LOCAL pose against the current parent (§15).
The attachment's world position (parent pose ∘ local). Writing it recomputes the LOCAL position against the current parent (§15).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptConnecti.documentation: One registered callback on a signal: Disconnect unregisters it, Connected reads back. Connections die with their creating script.
Whether the connection is still registered: false after Disconnect, after a Once connection fires, and after the owning script stops.
Unregisters the callback; Connected reads false afterward. Safe to call more than once.
Deprecated: the retired spelling of Connected, answered the same way — use Connected.
Deprecated: the retired spelling of Disconnect, answered the same way — use Disconnect.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.documentation: The event surface (the BV spelling of the reference engine's RBXScriptSignal): Connect and Once register callbacks, Wait suspends until the next fire. Delivery is deferred to the script pass after the event.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.C.documentation: Registers callback for every fire and returns the connection. The callback receives the signal's fired arguments; delivery is deferred to the script pass after the event.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.O.documentation: Like Connect, but the connection disconnects itself the moment it fires; the already-queued callback still runs.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.W.documentation: Suspends the calling thread until the next fire, then returns the fired arguments.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.c.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Connect, answered the same way — use Connect.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BVScriptSignal.w.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Wait, answered the same way — use Wait.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BallSocketConstr.documentation: A ball and socket: the two attachments held at one point, free to turn about it — while LimitsEnabled, Attachment1's X axis within UpperAngle of Attachment0's (a hard stop, measured), and with TwistLimitsEnabled its twist within TwistLowerAngle and TwistUpperAngle.
Whether the ball socket acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored (an anchored end leaves it active). Read only.
Whether Attachment1's X axis stops hard within UpperAngle of Attachment0's — the tilt cone (measured a hard limit) — and, with TwistLimitsEnabled, its twist within the twist range. Default false.

The socket's friction torque. Reads 0, the default; a write of any other value is refused: the reference's friction holds the attachments' angle against a smaller load (measured) and the engine's solver has no such hold (not supported in v1).
The size of the ball socket's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.15.

The cone's bounce, clamped to 0..1 at the write (measured), an infinity included; a NaN write is refused. Stored and saved, but inert: the socket stops dead at its limits whatever it holds (a recorded divergence, as the hinge's). Default 0.

Whether the twist — the angle from Attachment0's Y axis to Attachment1's about their X — stops hard within TwistLowerAngle and TwistUpperAngle. One of the limits: it acts while LimitsEnabled is on too. Default false.

The twist's lower limit in degrees, while TwistLimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write (measured), an infinity included; never reordered against TwistUpperAngle (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default -45.

The twist's upper limit in degrees, while TwistLimitsEnabled (a 20 rad/s twist under ±10 stopped at 12.1 — measured). Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included, never reordered against TwistLowerAngle (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

The tilt cone's half angle in degrees, while LimitsEnabled: the most Attachment1's X axis turns from Attachment0's (a hung arm pushed hard stopped at 30.9 under 30 — measured). Clamped to 0..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.documentation: Everything physical: world pose (Position, Rotation, CFrame), Size, appearance (Color, Material, Transparency), collision flags, and the Touched signal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Anchore.documentation: Whether the part is pinned in place. Anchored parts never simulate — no gravity, no forces — but still collide and fire Touched.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.ApplyAn.documentation: Instant spin change on the assembly's body: the angular impulse in world axes through the assembly's inertia (delta-omega = I⁻¹ · impulse). Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored assemblies.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.ApplyIm.documentation: Instant velocity change on the assembly's body: delta-v equals impulse divided by the assembly mass. Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored (infinite-mass) assemblies.

An impulse applied at a world position: the linear change of ApplyImpulse plus the spin its torque arm from the assembly's center of mass gives ((position - center) × impulse). Wakes a resting body. A no-op on anchored assemblies.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Assembl.documentation: The assembly's angular velocity in radians per second about the world axes — welded members answer, and set, their assembly root's. A write reads back at once; on an anchored assembly it lands in the property and the solver ignores it.
The assembly's center of mass in WORLD space: the mass-weighted center of every welded member, carried by the root's pose. Read only.
The assembly's linear velocity — welded members answer their assembly root's. Reads are zero without a live body; writes on anchored parts land but the solver ignores them.
The whole assembly's mass, every welded member's own summed; infinity for an anchored assembly. Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.BrickCo.documentation: The nearest BrickColor of the part's Color (the rule of BrickColor.new(color)); a write stores the table colour's bytes as Color3.fromRGB would, so Color reads back equal to fromRGB of them — an ulp off the BrickColor's own Color, as measured. Every real change of the colour fires Changed("BrickColor") and the BrickColor property signal before Color's pair; the same value again fires nothing. A BrickColor only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CFrame.documentation: The full rigid transform as one CFrame. Reads and writes agree with Position and Rotation — three views of the same pose. Welded members refuse the write; move the assembly root instead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CanColl.documentation: Whether the part responds to contacts. false keeps it physical — it falls and fires Touched — but removes the contact response.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CastSha.documentation: Whether the part casts a shadow (true by default), under the sun and under a PointLight or SpotLight whose Shadows is on. A part that casts none still receives the shadows of others. A server's write replicates like any other property's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.CenterO.documentation: The part's own center of mass in its LOCAL frame — the origin for every symmetric shape. Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Color.documentation: The authored surface color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.GetMass.documentation: The part's own mass — the Mass property as a method.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.GetNetw.documentation: Server-only: the player currently simulating this assembly, or nil for the server. Resolved through the assembly root.
Server-only: whether automatic (distance-based) ownership is in effect for this assembly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.GetRend.documentation: The world pose the part is DRAWN at this frame, which differs from CFrame while the render departs from the simulation under server authority: a correction's offset decaying, or a tick mover shown one tick behind (net-sync-v2 §2.9). A camera or an effect that must sit on what is on screen reads this in the render step; game logic reads CFrame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Locked.documentation: Whether the editor's viewport leaves the part alone: a click does not select a locked part and a box does not take it (the Explorer still selects it). Nothing at run time reads it; a server's write replicates like any other property's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Mass.documentation: The part's own mass: its material's density (the reference's numbers — Plastic 0.7, Metal 7.85, …) times its shape's volume. Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Materia.documentation: The surface material, as an Enum.Material item; writes accept the item or its string name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Positio.documentation: The part's world position. Welded members read their world pose, and a write moves the whole assembly with offsets preserved. Explicit writes fire the pose property signals; physics motion does not.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.RotVelo.documentation: Deprecated: the assembly's angular velocity in radians per second about the world axes — use AssemblyAngularVelocity. A write sets it and keeps the velocity of the assembly root part's position (measured), where an AssemblyAngularVelocity write keeps the centre of mass's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Rotatio.documentation: The orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees. Welded members read their assembly pose; writing a welded member is refused — rotate the assembly root instead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.SetNetw.documentation: Server-only: pins which peer simulates this assembly (nil means the server) and turns automatic ownership off. A non-Player instance degrades silently to the server. The part must be an unanchored workspace descendant.
Server-only: re-arms automatic (distance-based) ownership without clearing the standing owner.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Size.documentation: The part's dimensions in studs. The collider and mesh re-derive on write; a MeshPart's geometry scales against its authored MeshSize.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Touched.documentation: Fires when another collider starts touching this part, with the other object. Exists on unparented parts too; fires once per contact start.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Transpa.documentation: How see-through the part renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePart.Velocit.documentation: Deprecated: the velocity of the part's own position — the assembly's linear velocity plus its spin's arm from the centre of mass (measured) — use AssemblyLinearVelocity. A write on any part of an assembly sets the velocity of the assembly root part's position, the spin kept; on a part alone the pair is the assembly's. Not signal-backed (the reference fires Changed; recorded).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BasePlayerGui.documentation: The per-player UI container layer; no members of its own here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseRemoteEvent.documentation: The remote-event layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.documentation: The runnable scripts: the Enabled/Disabled run switch and RunContext, which decides where the code executes.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.Disab.documentation: The legacy inverse of Enabled — the two always mirror each other.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.Enabl.documentation: The script's run switch. Disabling kills the script's threads and listeners before the next pass; re-enabling restarts it fresh from the top. Writes require a real boolean (the reference engine coerces — a recorded strict-typing divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BaseScript.RunCo.documentation: Where the script runs: Legacy (placement decides), Server, or Client. Writes accept the enum item or its name string and re-derive execution immediately. A LocalScript's stored value is inert — its class decides.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.documentation: A world-anchored UI root: its elements render at its parent's position, facing the camera.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Anc.documentation: Which point of the billboard (0..1 per axis) its Position pins. A Vector2, like every GuiObject's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Pos.documentation: The billboard's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BillboardGui.Siz.documentation: The billboard's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.documentation: A same-context signal object: Fire queues Event for every listener — script-to-script signaling without the network.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.Ev.documentation: The receiving side of Fire: listeners get the fired arguments. Delivery is deferred to the next script pass; arguments pass by reference within the shared VM (the reference engine deep-copies — a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableEvent.Fi.documentation: Queues Event with these arguments for every listener, delivered on the next script pass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BindableFunction.documentation: A same-context call object: Invoke runs the assigned OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results.
Calls OnInvoke synchronously and returns its results (multiple returns pass through). Errors when OnInvoke is unset (the reference engine blocks forever — a recorded divergence).
The handler Invoke calls. Assign a function or nil; unset reads nil, and calling Invoke while unset errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BoolValue.documentation: A named container for one boolean.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BoolValue.Value.documentation: The stored boolean. Writes require a real boolean.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.documentation: A named colour of the reference engine's 208-entry table — its Number, its Name (what tostring prints), its Color and the three channels r, g, b; immutable, equal by value. BrickColor.new takes a number, a name, three channels or a Color3 (the nearest colour), palette(i) reads the 128-entry palette, random() draws from it, and eight named constructors (White, Gray, DarkGray, Black, Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) stand for their numbers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.Color.documentation: The colour as a Color3: each byte times 1/255 in single precision — an ulp off Color3.fromRGB's byte / 255 on some bytes (measured: BrickColor.new(21).Color ~= Color3.fromRGB(196, 40, 28)).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.Name.documentation: The colour's name — what tostring prints; case-sensitive in BrickColor.new.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.Numbe.documentation: The colour's number in the table, 1 to 1032 (194 is Medium stone grey, the answer for an unknown number or name).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.b.documentation: The blue channel, 0..1: the byte times 1/255.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.g.documentation: The green channel, 0..1: the byte times 1/255.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/BrickColor.r.documentation: The red channel, 0..1: the byte times 1/255.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.documentation: An immutable rigid transform: position plus rotation, right-handed and Y-up, with LookVector along -Z. Every operation returns a new value; cf1 * cf2 composes and cf * vector transforms the point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.AngleBetw.documentation: The angle in radians of the rotation from this CFrame's to other's, 0..π, positions ignored (single precision: a difference of 1e-4 reads 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.FuzzyEq.documentation: Whether other is this CFrame within eps (default 1e-5, at most 0.1): each position component within eps·(1 + |x|) of this frame's, the rotation between them within eps radians.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.GetCompon.documentation: The twelve numbers of the CFrame: the position, then the rotation matrix row by row (x, y, z, R00, R01, R02, R10, R11, R12, R20, R21, R22) — what the twelve-number CFrame.new takes back.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Inverse.documentation: The inverse transform: composing with it yields the identity.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Lerp.documentation: Interpolates toward goal: linear on position, slerp on rotation. Alpha is unclamped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.LookVecto.documentation: The facing direction: the -Z basis vector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Orthonorm.documentation: The CFrame with its rotation brought back to unit length. A CFrame here is always a position and a rotation — a matrix is orthonormalized as it is built (the reference keeps it as given) — so this undoes only the drift of long chains of products.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.PointToOb.documentation: Each world-space point as an object-space point — one value per argument, the inverse's position for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.PointToWo.documentation: Each object-space point as a world-space point — one value per argument, the position for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.Rotation.documentation: A rotation-only copy of this CFrame, with the translation stripped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToAxisAng.documentation: The rotation as an axis and an angle in radians: the angle 2·acos(w) in single precision, never negative; the identity's axis is (1, 0, 0) and its angle 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToEulerAn.documentation: The rotation as Euler angles in radians for an order (an Enum.RotationOrder item, XYZ by default), handed back as rx, ry, rz whatever the order.
The rotation as XYZ Euler angles in radians (the same order the instance Rotation property uses, in degrees there).
The rotation as YXZ Euler angles in radians — the angles of the Ry·Rx·Rz product, handed back as rx, ry, rz; at the lock rz is 0 and ry takes the sum or the difference.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToObjectS.documentation: Each world transform other, re-expressed relative to this CFrame (self:Inverse() * other) — one value per argument, the inverse for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToOrienta.documentation: ToEulerAnglesYXZ under its other name: rx, ry, rz of the Ry·Rx·Rz product, in radians.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ToWorldSp.documentation: Composes: each other, expressed relative to this CFrame, as a world transform (self * other) — one value per argument, this CFrame itself for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.VectorToO.documentation: Rotates each world direction into object space (no translation) — one value per argument, the zero vector for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.VectorToW.documentation: Rotates each direction into world space (no translation) — one value per argument, the zero vector for none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.XVector.documentation: The rotation matrix's first column: RightVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.YVector.documentation: The rotation matrix's second column: UpVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.ZVector.documentation: The rotation matrix's third column: the negated LookVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.component.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of GetComponents, answered the same way (measured) — use GetComponents.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.inverse.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Inverse (measured) — use Inverse.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.lerp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Lerp (measured) — use Lerp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.lookVecto.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of LookVector (measured) — use LookVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.p.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Position, answered the same way (measured) — use Position.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.pointToOb.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of PointToObjectSpace (measured) — use PointToObjectSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.pointToWo.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of PointToWorldSpace (measured) — use PointToWorldSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.rightVect.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of RightVector (measured) — use RightVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.toAxisAng.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToAxisAngle (measured) — use ToAxisAngle.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.toEulerAn.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToEulerAnglesXYZ (measured) — use ToEulerAnglesXYZ.
Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToEulerAnglesYXZ (measured) — use ToEulerAnglesYXZ.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.toObjectS.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToObjectSpace, its tuples too (measured) — use ToObjectSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.toOrienta.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToOrientation (measured) — use ToOrientation.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.toWorldSp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of ToWorldSpace, its tuples too (measured) — use ToWorldSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.upVector.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of UpVector (measured) — use UpVector.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.vectorToO.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of VectorToObjectSpace (measured) — use VectorToObjectSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.vectorToW.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of VectorToWorldSpace (measured) — use VectorToWorldSpace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.x.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of X (measured) — use X.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.y.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Y (measured) — use Y.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CFrame.z.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Z (measured) — use Z.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.documentation: The eye as an object: workspace.CurrentCamera is the one the process renders through (minted with the local player, none on a dedicated server); Instance.new makes further, inert cameras that CurrentCamera can be assigned. CameraType picks who drives it — the built-in orbit around CameraSubject in its several flavors, or scripts through CFrame — FieldOfView and its mode the lens, and the projection methods map between world and screen. Client-local: never saved or replicated.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CFrame.documentation: The eye's pose. Live in Custom — the orbit writes it every frame, and a script write re-seats the orbit from the written look direction at the current zoom (measured); authoritative in Scriptable. A script write fires the CFrame signal; the eye's own motion never does.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CameraSub.documentation: What the following modes track: any instance, though only one with a world pose (a part, a model, a character) or a Humanoid (followed through its body) moves the eye. The default is the local player's character's Humanoid (measured), and a nil write changes nothing — whatever subject was in place stays (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.CameraTyp.documentation: Who drives the camera. Custom (the play default) and Track are the built-in orbit around CameraSubject; Follow is that orbit swinging behind the subject's movement; Orbital the orbit at a locked zoom that ignores CFrame writes; Attach rides the subject and turns with it; Watch stays put and turns to face it; Fixed stays exactly where scripts put it and leaves Focus alone; Scriptable obeys CFrame writes and nothing else. Writes accept the item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.DiagonalF.documentation: The view across the viewport's diagonal, derived from FieldOfView and the viewport aspect by the reference engine's measured relation (tan(d/2) = tan²(v/2) + tan²(h/2)); a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.FieldOfVi.documentation: The VERTICAL field of view in degrees, clamped 1..120 (measured: 500 reads back 120, 0 reads back 1); default 70. A write fires this name and the two derived views.

Which view a viewport resize preserves — Vertical (the default: FieldOfView itself), Diagonal or MaxAxis — with the vertical recomputed to keep it. FieldOfView always reads the vertical value whatever the mode (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.Focus.documentation: The point of interest. The eye keeps it on the subject in every following mode (identity rotation), twenty studs ahead of the eye in Scriptable — where a script's own write is overridden the next frame (measured) — and untouched in Fixed.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.GetPartsO.documentation: Every part between the camera's position and any of the cast points — visible or not, collidable or not, the part around the point included — minus the ignore list with its descendants and the local player's character (measured); each part once.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.GetRender.documentation: The pose the eye actually renders from — the camera's CFrame (the two differ only under VR head tracking).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.HeadLocke.documentation: Whether VR head tracking follows the camera (default true). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.HeadScale.documentation: The VR head-to-world scale (default 1). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.MaxAxisFi.documentation: The view along the viewport's larger axis — horizontal in landscape, the vertical itself in portrait; a write sets the vertical that reads back as it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.NearPlane.documentation: The near clipping plane's z in the camera's own space: the negated near distance (−0.1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ScreenPoi.documentation: The unit ray through a screen pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals ViewportPointToRay.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.VRTiltAnd.documentation: Whether VR tilt and roll reach the camera (default false). Stored for parity; the engine renders no VR.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ViewportP.documentation: The unit ray through a viewport pixel, its origin on the near plane pushed depth studs along it (default 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ViewportS.documentation: The size of the view in pixels as a Vector2 (width, height). 1×1 for a camera no eye renders through. Fires its signal on a resize.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.WorldToSc.documentation: The pixel position of a world point as (x, y, depth) — depth the distance along the look, negative behind the eye — plus whether it is on screen. The engine has no GUI inset, so this equals WorldToViewportPoint.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.WorldToVi.documentation: The viewport position of a world point as (x, y, depth) in pixels from the top-left, plus whether it is inside the view and in front of the eye.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Camera.ZoomToExt.documentation: Backs the camera along its current look until the box's bounding sphere fits the view (radius over the sine of half the max-axis view — measured); a CFrame write like any other, so the orbit modes re-seat from it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.documentation: A live character body — the physical, scriptable entity a player controls, or an NPC from SpawnCharacter. One collidable part that stands in for the reference's whole rig: its pose surface and Touched are here, its brain is the Humanoid child (character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") — the body IS the part, so hit:FindFirstChildOfClass, not hit.Parent).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Assemb.documentation: The character body's center of mass in world space.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.CFrame.documentation: The character's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Center.documentation: The character body's local center of mass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Positi.documentation: The character's world position. Writing teleports the character.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.RotVel.documentation: Deprecated: the character body's angular velocity — use AssemblyAngularVelocity.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Rotati.documentation: The character's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees; writing turns the character.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Touche.documentation: Fires when a collider starts touching the character body, with the other object.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Character.Veloci.documentation: Deprecated: the character body's linear velocity — use AssemblyLinearVelocity.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.documentation: Makes its parent part clickable: MouseClick fires with the clicking player, within MaxActivationDistance.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.Ma.documentation: How far away (in studs) a player can be and still click, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ClickDetector.Mo.documentation: Fires when a player clicks the detector's parent part within MaxActivationDistance, with the clicking player. The signal lives on the detector, never on the part it makes clickable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/CollectionServic.documentation: Instance tags: storage is per-instance and survives leaving the tree, while GetTagged and the per-tag Added/Removed signals track tree membership. Tags serialize with the place.
Tags the instance (idempotent and silent on a duplicate). If it is in the game tree, the tag's Added signal fires.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.
The tag's membership signal: fires with each tagged instance that is (or becomes) part of the game tree.
The other half: fires (once) when a tagged instance leaves the tree — tag removed in-tree, detached, or destroyed.
Every instance in the game tree carrying the tag — tree membership, not storage: stored instances and husks stay out.
The instance's tags in add order.
Whether the instance carries the tag. Storage is per-instance and survives leaving the tree — and Destroy (husks keep their tags).
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).
Removes the tag (a no-op when absent). In-tree removals fire the tag's Removed signal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.documentation: An immutable RGB color with sRGB components 0..1. Color properties hand these out; their setters also keep accepting raw RGB vectors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.Lerp.documentation: Interpolates each component toward goal. Alpha is unclamped.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.ToHSV.documentation: Hue, saturation and value, each 0..1, of the channels clamped to 0..1. A grey's hue is 0; a saturated color whose hue is 0 reads 1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.ToHex.documentation: The color as six lowercase hex digits: each channel clamped to 0..1 and rounded half up to a byte. A NaN channel is an error.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Color3.lerp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Lerp, answered the same way (measured) — use Lerp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequence.documentation: A piecewise-linear color ramp over a unit time span, built from 2 to 20 keypoints under the same rules as NumberSequence — the particle Color.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequence.Ke.documentation: The keypoints in time order — a fresh table on every read, as the reference hands out.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ColorSequenceKey.documentation: One ColorSequence keypoint: Time and its Color3 Value.
The keypoint's position along the sequence, 0..1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.documentation: The base of the attachment-anchored constraints: Attachment0, Attachment1 and Enabled. A constraint acts while Enabled and the ends it needs sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.Attac.documentation: One end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil. The constraint acts while Enabled and both ends sit under live in-world parts; anything else is inert, never an error (§16). A destroyed attachment stays referenced.
The other end of the constraint: an Attachment or nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Constraint.Enabl.documentation: Whether the constraint acts. Disabling is inert (a joint's derived joint goes away, a mover pushes nothing); re-enabling rebuilds a joint at the current poses (§16).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.documentation: The `game` global: the service registry at the top of everything (measured ancestry DataModel < ServiceProvider < Instance). GetService hands out the engine services; PlaceId, GameId and JobId name the session; its Name is the place name ("Game" until the engine carries one — a recorded stub).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.BindTo.documentation: Binds a function the session's close calls with its Enum.CloseReason (DeveloperShutdown for the editor's Stop and a dedicated server's shutdown). The close lets every player go first — their PlayerRemoving fires — then starts every bound function at once, in bind order, each on a thread of its own; it waits for them to return, 30 seconds at most. One that raises stops none of the others; a script that died takes its binding with it. The server's alone.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.ClassN.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Collec.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.DataSt.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Debris.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.GameId.documentation: The game's id: what a dedicated server was started with (--game-id), the same on its clients; 0 where nothing names one. A client reads 0 until its join's world globals land.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.GetSer.documentation: Hands out an engine service by name ("Players", "RunService", "TweenService", …; "Workspace" answers the workspace root). Unknown names error.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.HttpSe.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.JobId.documentation: The running server's id: a fresh random UUID at every start of a dedicated server, read by the server and its clients alike; the empty string on the server side of the editor's Play and its session, where a client-side read answers the zero GUID (00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000) — Studio's pair, measured. A client reads the zero GUID until its join's world globals land.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Lighti.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Messag.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.PlaceI.documentation: The place's id: what a dedicated server was started with (--place-id), the same on its clients; 0 where nothing names one — the editor's Play and its session (a place here has no published identity). A client reads 0 until its join's world globals land.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Player.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Replic.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.RunSer.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Server.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).
The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.SoundS.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Starte.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).
The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.TweenS.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.UserIn.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.Worksp.documentation: The service as a field — the same value GetService answers for the name (the reference allows both spellings).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataModel.servic.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of GetService, answered the same way — use GetService.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.documentation: A global store's object (identity DataStore < GlobalDataStore, an Instance whose Parent is the DataStoreService): the key-value calls, each answer beside a DataStoreKeyInfo, and every version of a key kept, listed and read back, beside the listing of its keys.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.GetAsy.documentation: The key's value and its DataStoreKeyInfo — NOTHING, zero values, for a key never written or removed (measured). Yields while the store answers. A number key is its text; on a store opened with AllScopes a key is `<scope>/<key>`. The options' UseCache changes nothing: the engine keeps no cache.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.GetVer.documentation: The value one version of the key held and that version's key info — nothing for a removal's version; a version the key never had raises `502: … Error code: 25 Reason: The provided version is not valid.` (measured). Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.Increm.documentation: Adds delta (1 by default, rounded to a whole number half away from zero; NaN the int32 minimum, -2147483648) to the key's number — an absent key counts from 0 — and answers the new value and its key info; a key holding anything but a number, NaN included, raises `502: … Error code: 24 Reason: Key value is not numeric.` (measured). An infinite delta raises `Unable to cast double to int` (the engine's). The options' metadata rides the write. Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.ListKe.documentation: The keys that start with prefix, sorted — a removed key too unless excludeDeleted is true (measured; false by default) — pageSize to a page (0: 50), after the cursor a key pages answered — every scope's as `<scope>/<key>` on a store opened with AllScopes; a cursor no listing answered raises `502: … Error code: 32 Reason: The provided exclusive start key is not valid.` (measured). Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.ListVe.documentation: Every version of the key — each write, a removal's marked deleted — oldest first unless sortDirection is Descending (measured), written between minDate and maxDate (Unix milliseconds, inclusive; 0 unbounded), pageSize to a page (0: 1024). Every write is kept as a version. The reference kept one version for three writes 7 s apart (measured 2026-10-16) yet two for two writes 0.3 s apart (measured 2026-10-07); the creator docs name a one-per-UTC-hour rule and a 30-day expiry, the window unmeasured. The engine merges and expires nothing. Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.Remove.documentation: Removes the key, writing a version marked deleted, and answers the removed value and its key info; a later GetAsync answers nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

Removes one version of the key and answers nothing; the version stays listed, IsDeleted true, and GetVersionAsync of it answers nothing — the newest too, after which the key answers nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.SetAsy.documentation: Writes the value (and the user ids, four at most, and the options' metadata, 300 bytes at most) as a new version and answers its version id. The value is kept as JSON — a mixed table keeps its array part, a sparse array or a fractional key becomes string keys, NaN and inf survive — and refused past 4 MB of it; a function, an Instance or a Vector3 cannot be stored (`104: Cannot store <Type> in data store. …`), and a nil value raises `Argument 2 missing or nil`, storing nothing (measured). Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStore.Update.documentation: Calls transform with the key's value and key info (nil, nil for a key with none) and stores what it returns — the value, the user ids, the metadata — answering the stored value and its key info; a transform returning nil writes nothing and the call answers one nil. A transform that yields (inside a pcall too) or errors is logged (`Transform function error Callbacks cannot yield`; the error with its stack, then `Transform function error <message>`) and the call answers nothing and raises nothing — the value stays; a yielded transform runs on when its wait wakes, its result discarded (measured). If the key changed under the transform, it runs again on the new value. Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreGetOpti.documentation: The options GetAsync reads: UseCache, true by default — the engine keeps no cache, so a read is fresh either way. Script-made, never saved.
Whether GetAsync may answer from a cache: true by default (measured). The engine keeps no cache, so a read is fresh either way.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreIncreme.documentation: The options IncrementAsync reads: the metadata SetMetadata gives rides the increment. Script-made, never saved.
The metadata SetMetadata gave — an empty table before it.
The metadata the next IncrementAsync with these options writes — a table, 300 bytes of JSON at most when the write lands.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreInfo.documentation: One written store, as ListDataStoresAsync lists it: its name and its first and latest write.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreInfo.Cr.documentation: The store's first write in any scope, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the session clock.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreInfo.Up.documentation: The store's latest write in any scope, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the session clock.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreKey.documentation: One key, as ListKeysAsync lists it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreKey.Key.documentation: The key — `<scope>/<key>` on a store opened with AllScopes.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreKeyInfo.documentation: What a store call answers beside a value: the version, the key's creation and the version's time (Unix milliseconds on the session clock), the user ids and the metadata the version was written with.
When the key was first written (or first written again after a removal), in milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the session clock.
The metadata this version was written with — an empty table when it set none (measured).
The user ids this version was written with, in order — an empty table when it named none (measured).
"Instance" — the name its tostring and its member error answer (measured).
When this version was written, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the session clock.
The version this answer describes, in the reference's shape `<created>.<sequence>.<updated>.01` over the engine's own numbers — compare it and hand it back, never parse it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreKeyPage.documentation: The pages of a store's keys (identity DataStoreKeyPages < Pages), with the Cursor a later ListKeysAsync continues from.

Where the next page starts — a base64 text the listing call takes back as its cursor (measured); "" on the last page.
The current page's items, a fresh table each call (measured).
Whether the current page is the last (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreListing.documentation: The pages of the written stores (identity DataStoreListingPages < Pages), with the Cursor a later ListDataStoresAsync continues from.

Where the next page starts — a base64 text the listing call takes back as its cursor (measured); "" on the last page.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreObjectV.documentation: One version of a key, as ListVersionsAsync lists it: its id, when it was written and whether it is a removal's.
When the version was written, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the session clock.
Whether the version is a removal's (measured: RemoveAsync writes one).
The version's id — GetVersionAsync and RemoveVersionAsync take it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreOptions.documentation: The options GetDataStore reads: AllScopes opens a store across every scope of its name (its keys `<scope>/<key>`), and SetExperimentalFeatures takes { v2 = true }. Script-made, never saved.

Whether GetDataStore opens the store across every scope of its name (false by default, measured) — then the scope must be "" (`DataStore scope should be an empty string allScopes is set to true`, nil meaning "global") and every key reads `<scope>/<key>`.
Takes the reference's feature switches; { v2 = true } is accepted and kept (measured) and changes nothing here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStorePages.documentation: The pages of an ordered store's entries sorted by value (identity DataStorePages < Pages), each entry a plain table { key, value }.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/DataStoreService.documentation: The data stores: GetDataStore and GetOrderedDataStore answer a store's object at once, the same one on every call; the object's calls (GetAsync, SetAsync, UpdateAsync, RemoveAsync, IncrementAsync, the versions and the key listing) and ListDataStoresAsync yield while the store answers. Values are kept as JSON with the reference's limits — 50-character names and keys, 4 MB values. The editor's Play keeps the open project's test store from one Play to the next; a dedicated server keeps its saves where --data-dir says, or none — every store call then raising a 403 text that says so. The server's alone: a client side's call raises.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.

The global store under name and scope ("global" by default) — the same object on every call. A name or scope is 1 to 50 characters (`DataStore name can't be empty string`, `DataStore name is too long`, `DataStore scope can't be empty string`, `DataStore scope is too long`); a number is its text. The options are a DataStoreOptions: with AllScopes the store spans every scope of the name, the scope must be "" and each key reads `<scope>/<key>` (another class `510: Options instance not of type DataStoreOptions`, a non-Instance `Unable to cast value to Object`). The server's alone — a client side's call raises `DataStore can't be accessed from client`. The editor's Play keeps the open project's test store for its next Play; a dedicated server keeps its saves where --data-dir says, or none — every call of a store object then raises `403: DataStore access is off: …`.
The experience's default store, named "". The server's alone.
The ordered store under name and scope — the same object on every call, the names refused as GetDataStore's. The server's alone.

How many requests of the type a fresh session may make — the measured constants on a server (688 GetAsync, 673 StandardWrite, 671 UpdateAsync, 40 GetSortedAsync, 33 ListAsync, 40 GetVersionAsync, 42 RemoveVersionAsync; 640 for the rest) and the client's own on a client (measured: 2500, 130 or 350 by type, 17 OnUpdate). The engine keeps no budget and throttles nothing: the answer never moves, where the reference's server budget does.
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

The global stores written in any scope whose name starts with prefix, sorted — an ordered store and one never written are not listed (measured) — pageSize to a page (0: 32), after the cursor a listing pages answered. Yields while the store answers. The server's alone — a client side's call raises `DataStore can't be accessed from client` (measured).
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.documentation: Scheduled destruction: AddItem destroys an instance after a lifetime on the pause-aware script clock — fire-and-forget cleanup for projectiles and effects.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.AddItem.documentation: Schedules the instance's destruction after `lifetime` seconds (default 10, negatives destroy promptly) on the pause-aware script clock. Re-adding an item replaces its timer.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.ClassName.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Debris.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enum.documentation: One enum of the tree, `Enum.<Type>`: its items by name, and GetEnumItems, FromName and FromValue; a name it has no item or method for is an error. A read-only table here (typeof "table").

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enum.FromName.documentation: The item with that name, or nil. The name must be a string: nothing else converts.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enum.FromValue.documentation: The item with that Value (the engine's numbering — see EnumItem.Value), the number truncated toward zero, or nil. The value must be a number: a numeric string does not convert.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enum.GetEnumItem.documentation: A fresh array of the enum's items, ascending by Value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.documentation: One `Enum.<Type>.<Item>` value: equality is by item, tostring prints the full path, and enum-valued properties accept the item or its plain name string.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.EnumTyp.documentation: The owning enum's name, as a string (the reference engine answers an Enum object here — a recorded divergence).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.Name.documentation: The item's name — the last segment of Enum.Material.Neon.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/EnumItem.Value.documentation: The item's numeric value: an engine-internal index, stable within a release but not a reference-engine value — except FontWeight (the reference's 100..900), RenderPriority (its 0..2000, the numbers BindToRenderStep takes) and Font (its 0..51 with Unknown 100, the api dump's).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enums.documentation: The `Enum` global: every enum by name, and GetEnums; a name it has no enum for is an error. A read-only table here (typeof "table").

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Enums.GetEnums.documentation: A fresh array of every enum of the tree, in name order.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Folder.documentation: A pure organizational container with no behavior of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.documentation: A typeface value: Family (a local font asset path; the empty string is the engine default face), Weight (Enum.FontWeight, Thin 100 to Heavy 900), Style (Normal or Italic) and Bold. The fields write, like the reference engine's; FontFace speaks it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Bold.documentation: Whether the weight is SemiBold or heavier; writing true sets Bold, false Regular (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Family.documentation: The typeface as a local font asset path (a .ttf/.otf under the assets root); the empty string is the engine default face, and so renders a reference catalog family (rbxasset://fonts/families/ …, what Font.fromEnum and the legacy Font property store), kept verbatim. Recorded divergence: the reference engine's Family is a cloud font-family URL.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Style.documentation: Normal (the default) or Italic. An enum item only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Font.Weight.documentation: The weight, Thin (100) to Heavy (900); Regular by default. An enum item only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/FormFactorPart.documentation: A legacy layer between BasePart and Part, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Frame.documentation: The plain rectangular UI element: a background and a parent for other elements.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiBase.documentation: The UI root layer, kept for ancestry parity with the reference engine.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiBase2d.documentation: The 2D UI layer beneath every on-screen element.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiButton.documentation: The clickable UI elements: Activated fires on click release.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiButton.Activa.documentation: Fires (with no arguments) when a click is released over the button.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiLabel.documentation: The display-only UI elements — the image and text labels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.documentation: The visible UI elements: UDim2 Position and Size, AnchorPoint, and the background fill.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Anchor.documentation: Which point of the element (0..1 per axis) its Position pins: (0, 0) the top-left corner, (0.5, 0.5) the center. A Vector2 — assigning anything else refuses (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Backgr.documentation: How see-through the element's fill renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Layout.documentation: The sibling sort key a parent's UIListLayout orders by (SortOrder.LayoutOrder); lower comes first. Ignored without a layout.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Positi.documentation: The element's position as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis), relative to the parent element.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Size.documentation: The element's size as a UDim2 (scale plus pixel offset per axis).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/GuiObject.Visibl.documentation: Whether the element renders. A hidden element hides its whole subtree and occupies no layout space.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HingeConstraint.documentation: A hinge: the two bodies rotate about the attachments' X axes — free, or driven by a Motor or a Servo (ActuatorType), within optional limits.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HingeConstraint..documentation: What drives the hinge: None (a free hinge, the default), Motor (turns at AngularVelocity) or Servo (turns to TargetAngle). Writes accept the Enum.ActuatorType item or its name.

How stiffly the Servo pulls toward its target: 5 approaches slowly, 45 (the default) arrives without overshoot, 200 overshoots against its torque cap. Stored within 5 to 200: a write outside lands on the nearer end, an infinite one included (measured); a NaN write is refused.
The Servo's rate cap in radians per second: its applied target moves toward TargetAngle by at most this much a second. The default 0 holds the Servo where it stands (measured).
The Motor's target speed in radians per second: Attachment1 turns about Attachment0's X axis at it, within MotorMaxTorque and MotorMaxAcceleration. Default 0.

The hinge's angle in degrees: Attachment1 about Attachment0's X axis, 0 with the two attachments aligned, positive turning Attachment0's Y toward its Z (measured). 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it turns.
Whether the hinge stops hard at LowerAngle and UpperAngle. Default false.
The lower limit in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default -45.
The Motor's angular-acceleration cap in radians per second squared: its applied speed ramps toward AngularVelocity by at most this much a second (measured as a true cap). Default 500000.
The most torque the Motor applies. The default 0 moves nothing (measured), as does any value of 0 or less.
The size of the hinge's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.15.

The limits' bounce, clamped to 0..1 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Stored and saved, but inert: the hinge stops dead at a limit whatever it holds (a recorded divergence — the reference bounces). Default 0.
The most torque the Servo applies. The default 0 moves nothing, as does any value of 0 or less.
Deprecated on the reference. Stored and saved, inert. Default false.
The Servo's target in degrees from the two attachments aligned, reduced modulo 360 and reached the short way (270 is -90, 720 is 0 — measured). Default 0.
The upper limit in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Clamped to -180..180 at the write, an infinity included (measured); a NaN write is refused. Default 45.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.documentation: The JSON codec (JSONEncode/JSONDecode) and random GUIDs, usable everywhere; the request verbs are closed — HttpEnabled is false and GetAsync/PostAsync/RequestAsync error, the engine sends no HTTP.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Clas.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.
