@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Gene.documentation: A random version-4 UUID in lowercase hexadecimal, 8-4-4-4-12, wrapped in curly braces unless wrapInCurlyBraces is false (a number counts by zero/nonzero, the strings "true"/"false" cast; anything else errors `Unable to cast <type> to bool`).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.GetA.documentation: Closed: errors `HTTP requests are not enabled. Enable via Experience Settings` — the engine sends no HTTP.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Http.documentation: Whether scripts may send HTTP requests: false — the engine has no outbound HTTP, and the reference lets only the place's settings write it. The JSON and GUID members work regardless.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.JSON.documentation: The JSON text as a value: null is nil, objects string-keyed tables (a null field absent, the tagged non-finite object its number), arrays 1-based tables, numbers doubles; a number argument is its text. Invalid text errors `Can't parse JSON`, nil `Argument 1 missing or nil`.

The value as compact JSON (measured): a table with a length is an array of 1..#t (holes null, other keys dropped), an empty table [], any other table an object — its keys a string, a number's integer text or `<Type> (tostring)` for the rest, written sorted; an integral number prints without a decimal point, a non-finite one as {"m":null,"t":"numeric","v":"inf"}; nil values are absent; a function, userdata, thread or vector encodes null. A cyclic table errors `tables cannot be cyclic`, a boolean key `Invalid table key type used`, a nest past 512 tables `Can't convert to JSON`.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Post.documentation: Closed: errors `HTTP requests are not enabled. Enable via Experience Settings` — the engine sends no HTTP.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/HttpService.Requ.documentation: Closed: errors `HTTP requests are not enabled. Enable via Experience Settings` — the engine sends no HTTP.
`options: { Url: string, Method: string?, Headers: { [string]: string }?, Body: string? }`
`{ Success: boolean, StatusCode: number, StatusMessage: string, Headers: { [string]: string }, Body: string }`

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.documentation: A character's brain, a child of the body it drives: Health and MaxHealth with Died and HealthChanged, WalkSpeed and JumpPower, the one-shot Jump, Sit and PlatformStand, MoveTo/Move with MoveDirection, WalkToPoint and MoveToFinished, and the state machine — GetState, StateChanged, Running, Jumping, FreeFalling, Seated, the SetStateEnabled gates. Spawned with every body; Instance.new makes a bodiless one (RootPart nil, state None) that parenting under a body brings alive. Destroying it leaves the body standing, and it never respawns (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Died.documentation: Fires once per life, when Health reaches zero, with the body still in the world.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Display.documentation: The name shown for the character: the body's name at spawn, empty for an Instance.new humanoid (measured). Up to 4096 bytes — the wire's limit; the reference caps nothing (recorded).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.FreeFal.documentation: true on entering Freefall and again on Landed (the reference's own quirk, measured); false on Landed and on the return to Running.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.GetMove.documentation: MoveDirection times WalkSpeed times the intent's length: (WalkSpeed, 0, 0) for Move(1, 0, 0), half for a half-length direction, the unit's y scaled too (measured); zero at rest.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.GetStat.documentation: The current state: Running, Jumping, Freefall, Landed, Seated, PlatformStanding or Dead on a body this end simulates; None for an unparented humanoid. A replica keeps the state it was born with (only the dead latch travels).
Whether SetStateEnabled left the state enabled (measured: every state starts enabled).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Health.documentation: Current health; a write clamps to 0..MaxHealth at once (measured). Reaching zero fires Died once and latches the humanoid dead — the body stays in the world until the respawn replaces it; a write on a dead humanoid reads back for the frame and is forced back to 0 on the next pass (measured) — nothing revives it. Every change fires HealthChanged, after the property's own Changed (measured order). A non-finite write is refused (the reference stores it — recorded).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.HealthC.documentation: Fires with the new Health on every change — and with the unchanged Health on a MaxHealth write (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Jump.documentation: A one-shot jump request: true makes the body take off on its next simulated tick (if grounded and Jumping is enabled) and reads back true until then; a seated humanoid stands up on it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.JumpPow.documentation: The upward velocity a jump imparts, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Jumping.documentation: true on takeoff, false the frame after (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.MaxHeal.documentation: The ceiling the Health SETTER clamps to, floored at 0 (math.huge accepted). Lowering it leaves the current Health alone (measured: 100 over a MaxHealth of 50 stays 100) and fires HealthChanged with it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Move.documentation: Sets a persistent world-space walk direction: the body keeps walking until the next call, a zero vector stops it, and the length scales the speed (half a unit walks at half WalkSpeed — measured). The relativeToCamera flag is client presentation and is ignored here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.MoveDir.documentation: The unit direction of the last accepted Move (the controls, on a possessed body), y included; zero at rest and zero during a MoveTo; kept through sitting and death, where a Move while seated is ignored (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.MoveTo.documentation: Walks the body to a point: reached within 1 stud in the horizontal plane, or given up after 8 seconds (every call restarts the timer). MoveToFinished fires with the outcome; a pending MoveTo owns locomotion over Move. With a part, the point is relative to it (WalkToPart) as it moves.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.MoveToF.documentation: Fires when a MoveTo ends: true when the target was reached, false on the timeout. A replaced target fires nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Platfor.documentation: Limp: no walking, no jumping, the PlatformStanding state (measured; skipped when SetStateEnabled turned it off); a false write returns the body to Running.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.RootPar.documentation: The body this humanoid drives — the one-part Character — or nil for a humanoid parented nowhere a body is (measured: nil fresh from Instance.new and in a Folder).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Running.documentation: Fires with the ground speed as it changes while Running — silent in the air — and with 0 on entering any other state (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.SeatPar.documentation: The seat occupied — always nil: no seat class exists yet; Sit seats in place.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Seated.documentation: Fires (true, nil) on sitting and (false, nil) on standing up — the seat nil until a seat class exists.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.SetStat.documentation: Keeps the state machine OUT of a state, never the motion (measured): Seated or PlatformStanding off skip the state while the body still cannot walk, Jumping off refuses the player's own jump but an NPC still takes off straight into Freefall, Dead off keeps a zero-health humanoid alive and unable to walk. Takes the item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Sit.documentation: Seated in place (no seat class exists yet, so SeatPart stays nil): the body walks nowhere and enters the Seated state with Seated(true, nil) — unless SetStateEnabled turned Seated off, when the state is skipped but the body still cannot walk (measured). A false write stands up; so does a jump on the player's own character (the reference's controls do that), while an NPC stays seated (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.StateCh.documentation: Fires (old, new) on every state transition, after the state's own signal. The capsule body walks Running, Jumping, Freefall, Landed, Seated, PlatformStanding and Dead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.TakeDam.documentation: Subtracts amount from Health, floored at zero — reaching zero fires Died; the body stays, dead, until the respawn replaces it. A negative amount heals, past MaxHealth too (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.Touched.documentation: Fires (touchingPart, humanoidPart) when a collider starts touching the body this humanoid drives — the toucher, then the one-part body (measured shape, once per contact start, silent at rest — relayed from the body's contacts).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.WalkSpe.documentation: The body's walk speed in studs per second, floored at 0 (measured: a negative write reads 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Humanoid.WalkToP.documentation: The part the last MoveTo target is relative to, or nil.
The last MoveTo target, kept after arrival (measured). Read-only here where the reference accepts a write — a recorded divergence.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ImageLabel.documentation: A UI element that displays an image asset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ImageLabel.Image.documentation: The displayed image, as a local asset path. Unset reads as the empty string; writing the empty string clears it.
Tints the image: each texel is multiplied by this color. White (the default) draws the image as authored.
How see-through the image itself renders (the background has its own transparency), clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.documentation: One typed input under an InputContext — Bool, Direction1D, Direction2D or Direction3D — driven by its InputBinding children every frame; GetState reads it, StateChanged/Pressed/Released fire on change.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Enab.documentation: Whether the action is driven by its bindings and Fire (true by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Fire.documentation: Writes the state from a script — a boolean, a number, a Vector2 or a Vector3 by the Type — firing StateChanged (and Pressed/Released for a Bool) on a real change. The way an action with no bindings is driven; bound actions are overwritten by their keys next frame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.GetS.documentation: The current state as the Type reads it: a boolean, a number in -1..1, a Vector2 or a Vector3 — driven every frame by the InputBinding children, or by Fire when there are none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Pres.documentation: Bool actions: fires with true when the state goes from released to pressed.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Rele.documentation: Bool actions: fires with false when the state goes from pressed to released.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Stat.documentation: Fires with the new state whenever it changes, never for a same-state write; a held direction fires once, so poll GetState for continuous input.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputAction.Type.documentation: What the action carries: Bool (a press), Direction1D (a number), Direction2D (a Vector2) or Direction3D (a Vector3). Writes accept the item or its name and reset the state.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.documentation: One key binding under an InputAction: KeyCode for a Bool or Direction1D action, the Up/Down/Left/Right/Forward/Backward keys for a directional one, modifiers that must be held, the output scales and the unit-length clamp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Bac.documentation: The composite key for +Z; None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Cla.documentation: Whether a composite direction longer than 1 (two keys at once) is clamped to unit length before the scales (true by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Dow.documentation: The composite key for -Y; None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.For.documentation: The composite key for -Z (a Direction3D's (0, 0, -1)); None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Key.documentation: The key driving a Bool action (pressed) or a Direction1D one (+1); None when unset. Writes accept the item, its name, or None (Unknown, its legacy name, too) to clear.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Lef.documentation: The composite key for -X (a Direction2D's (-1, 0)); None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Pri.documentation: A key that must be held for the binding to count; None (the default) requires none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Rig.documentation: The composite key for +X; None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Sca.documentation: A multiplier on every component of a directional action's output (1 by default), applied after the clamp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Sec.documentation: A second key that must be held for the binding to count; None (the default) requires none.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Up.documentation: The composite key for +Y (a Direction1D's +1, a Direction2D's (0, 1), a Direction3D's (0, 1, 0)); None when unset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputBinding.Vec.documentation: A per-component multiplier on a Direction2D action's output ((1, 1) by default), applied after the clamp.
A per-component multiplier on a Direction3D action's output ((1, 1, 1) by default), applied after the clamp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputContext.documentation: A group of InputActions: contexts are read in descending Priority, and a Sink context consumes the keys its bindings use before lower-priority contexts see them. Under a Player, its actions' states reach the server.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputContext.Ena.documentation: Whether the context's actions are read at all (true by default). A disabled context's actions hold their last state.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputContext.Pri.documentation: Contexts are read in descending priority (0 by default; an integer, a fraction truncates): a higher context's Sink consumes keys before a lower one sees them.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/InputContext.Sin.documentation: When true, the keys this context's bindings read are consumed at its priority and never reach lower-priority contexts (false by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.documentation: The root of the class tree: identity (Name, ClassName), the Parent tree with its hierarchy signals, attributes, and lifetime (Clone, Destroy). Every scriptable object is an Instance.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Ancestr.documentation: Fires when this instance or any ancestor is reparented, on every node of the moved subtree (deepest first), with the MOVED instance and its new parent — nil on detach. Destroy fires each destroyed node's own (self, nil).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Archiva.documentation: Whether Clone copies the instance: true by default. A non-archivable instance's Clone returns nil, and a clone of its parent leaves it and its subtree out; a character is born non-archivable. A runtime flag: neither saved nor replicated, never copied by Clone, and a boolean only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Attribu.documentation: Fires with the attribute NAME on every landed attribute write — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Delivers once per landed write in write order, before the matching GetAttributeChangedSignal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Changed.documentation: Fires with the property NAME on every landed property write — pose writes fan out to CFrame, Position and Rotation; same-value writes stay silent; attribute writes travel their own AttributeChanged channel; physics motion never fires. The value containers override it entirely: their Changed fires only for Value, with the new VALUE as payload.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ChildAd.documentation: Fires when an instance is parented directly under this one. The listener receives the added child.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ChildRe.documentation: Fires when a direct child is unparented from this instance or destroyed. The listener receives the removed child.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ClassNa.documentation: The instance's class, as a string. An instance never changes class. Prefer IsA over comparing ClassName — IsA also matches base classes like BasePart.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.ClearAl.documentation: Destroys every direct child and its subtree — the last child first, each node's Destroying before its children's — and leaves the instance itself in place. The cleared nodes are husks: parentless and locked. On a destroyed instance it does nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Clone.documentation: A deep copy of the instance and its subtree: authored state, attributes and tags copy; the copy is detached (Parent is nil) with fresh identity. A destroyed instance clones its husk as a live single-node copy.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Descend.documentation: Fires when an instance is added anywhere in this instance's subtree, with the added descendant. When a whole subtree is attached it fires for the attached node itself, not for every instance below it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Destroy.documentation: Destroys the instance and its whole subtree, firing Destroying. Destroyed instances stay readable as husks: properties read their last values, Parent reads nil and is locked. Destroying an already-destroyed instance does nothing.
Fires when the instance is destroyed. The listener sees a husk: properties still read their last values, the tree is severed, and Parent reads nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.FindFir.documentation: The nearest ancestor named name, or nil. The chain ends at the DataModel: game's Name matches last (measured).
The nearest ancestor whose ClassName is exactly className, or nil. FindFirstAncestorOfClass("DataModel") answers game from any rooted instance (measured).
The nearest ancestor that IsA(className), or nil — game answers for DataModel, ServiceProvider and (with no nearer match) Instance, its measured ancestry.
The first direct child named name, or nil. The cheap probe when absence is an expected answer — cache the result instead of re-finding it every frame.
The first direct child whose ClassName is exactly className, or nil. Never recursive (measured: a second argument is ignored) — FindFirstChildWhichIsA is the one that descends.
The first direct child that IsA(className), or nil; with recursive true the whole subtree is searched in GetDescendants order.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetAttr.documentation: The named attribute — a bare value for primitives, a table of fields for records — or nil when unset. The two-argument form is a BetterVoxel extension: it projects one field of a record as a bare value without building the table — the cheap shape for hot loops (nil on primitives).

A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named attribute lands a change on this instance — first set, value changes and removal included; same-value writes stay silent. Any attribute name is legal, set or not. Delivers after the instance-wide AttributeChanged for the same write.

Every attribute of the instance as a fresh table of name to value — a bare value for primitives, a table of fields for records — empty when none is set. The table is a copy: writing it changes no attribute (SetAttribute does).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetChil.documentation: The direct children, in child order, as an array. A destroyed instance answers an empty array.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetDesc.documentation: Every instance below this one as an array, in preorder: each node comes before its own children.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetFull.documentation: The instance's full dot-joined path from the root, Workspace included: 'Workspace.Folder.Part'. A detached instance's full name is just its Name — member errors quote this same spelling.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.GetProp.documentation: A signal that fires (with no arguments) when the named property changes on this instance. Explicit writes fire it; physics motion never fires the pose properties. Subscribing errors when the property can never fire on this class — the same catch-the-typo philosophy as unknown member names.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.IsA.documentation: Whether the instance's class is className or inherits from it: a Part IsA 'BasePart' and IsA 'Instance'. Unknown class names answer false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.IsAnces.documentation: Whether this instance sits anywhere above descendant (self does not count; nil answers false — measured, asymmetric with IsDescendantOf).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.IsDesce.documentation: Whether ancestor sits anywhere above this instance (self does not count). game counts for every rooted instance, and nil answers TRUE — the measured quirk: every chain ends at nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Name.documentation: The instance's name — the label the Explorer shows and the key FindFirstChild, WaitForChild and dot-child access match on. Names need not be unique among siblings; lookups return the first match in child order.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Parent.documentation: The instance's parent in the object tree, or nil for a detached root; a Player's is the Players service while it is in the game (measured). Assigning Parent reparents without moving anything in world space; assigning nil detaches the subtree without destroying it. Locked after Destroy.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Predict.documentation: Whether a client predicts this instance under server authority (net-sync-v2 §2.9): Automatic unless RunService:SetPredictionMode forced it On or Off on this client. Read-only; the reference shows it in Studio only under server authority.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.Remove.documentation: Deprecated: sets the Parent of this instance and of every descendant to nil, top-down, each node leaving with the ordinary signals of a reparent. Nothing is destroyed or locked: every node can take a parent again. On a destroyed instance it does nothing. Use Destroy to destroy, or set Parent to nil to detach.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.SetAttr.documentation: Writes the named attribute: a primitive or datatype (Vector3, Color3, CFrame) stores directly, a table stores a structured record, and nil REMOVES the attribute (also the way to change its type: remove, then set). Writes coerce onto the attribute's declared shape — out-of-range values error, a record write merges field by field with missing fields keeping their values. Every landed write fires AttributeChanged then the per-name signal; same-value writes are silent. Names are capped at 100 characters and cannot be empty; non-finite components refuse.
`value: boolean | number | string | Vector3 | Color3 | CFrame | {[string]: any} | nil`

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.WaitFor.documentation: The first direct child named name, suspending the calling thread until one exists. A child already present returns without yielding. With a timeout (in seconds) the wait gives up and returns nil once it elapses; without one it waits forever.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.changed.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Changed, answered the same way — a value container's is its value signal — use Changed.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.clone.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Clone, answered the same way — use Clone.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.destroy.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Destroy, answered the same way — use Destroy.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.findFir.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of FindFirstChild, answered the same way — use FindFirstChild.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Instance.remove.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of Remove, answered the same way.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/IntValue.documentation: A named container for one integer; number writes round half away from zero.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/IntValue.Value.documentation: The stored integer. Number writes round half away from zero (3.5 becomes 4, -3.7 becomes -4).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.documentation: The base of the classic joints: Part0 and Part1, the frames C0 and C1 they are held at, Enabled, and the read-only Active.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.Ac.documentation: Whether the joint acts: Enabled, parented in the tree, both ends set to two different parts in the tree, and not both of them anchored (two anchored parts each root an assembly of their own; measured, §43).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.C0.documentation: The joint's frame in Part0's space: while Active, Part0.CFrame * C0 equals Part1.CFrame * C1. Writing it moves the part that is not the assembly root on the next physics pass (measured, §43).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.C1.documentation: The joint's frame in Part1's space — C0's counterpart.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.En.documentation: Whether the joint may act (Active also needs both ends). Disabling leaves the parts where they stand; re-enabling stands the non-root part where C0 and C1 put it (measured, §43).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/JointInstance.Pa.documentation: The part C0 is a frame of: an Instance or nil. Setting an end of an active joint moves the part that is not the assembly root to where the frames put it (§43).
The part C1 is a frame of: an Instance or nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LayerCollector.documentation: The UI roots that collect an element tree: ScreenGui on the screen, BillboardGui in the world.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.documentation: The shared light surface: Brightness, Color, Range, Shadows and the Enabled switch, parented under the part that carries the light.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Brightness.documentation: The light's intensity, floored at 0. The unit is the renderer's (a default light reads 1000000), not the reference engine's 0..~10 scale — a recorded divergence.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Color.documentation: The light's color. Writes accept a Color3 or a raw RGB vector (sRGB components 0..1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Enabled.documentation: Whether the light is lit. Disabling removes the derived render light; the authored properties keep their values.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Light.Range.documentation: How far the light reaches, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.documentation: The global lighting state: ambient color, sun brightness, the ClockTime day cycle, and distance fog. The skybox is file-authored in v1 — scripts move the sun, not the sky.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Ambient.documentation: The ambient light color, filling in where no light reaches. Accepts a Color3 or a raw RGB vector, like every color setter.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.ClassNa.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.ClockTi.documentation: The time of day in hours: writes clamp onto 0..24 and 24 reads back as 0 (the measured reference contract); the sun and sky follow.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Exposur.documentation: A bias to the scene's exposure before the tone curve, in stops: 1 is twice the light, -1 half. Writes clamp onto -5..5, the range the reference states; a non-finite number is refused.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.FogEnd.documentation: The distance where fog fully occludes, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.FogStar.documentation: The distance where fog begins, in studs, floored at 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Geograp.documentation: Degrees north, clamped to -90..90. The sun follows the reference's measured model — the day circle plus a tan(latitude - 23.5) north-lean — so at the engine default 0 (Roblox defaults to 41.733) the noon sun leans 23.5 degrees south, and latitude 23.5 puts it overhead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.GetSunD.documentation: The unit direction toward the sun for the current ClockTime and GeographicLatitude.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.GlobalS.documentation: Whether the sun casts shadows. Turn it off (with Brightness 0) for a fully unlit look.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Lighting.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.documentation: A mover: a force that brings Attachment0's assembly to a velocity within each physics step — the whole vector, its component along a line, or its projection on a plane, named in RelativeTo's frame — within its force limits, the assembly's weight held.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.A.documentation: Whether the velocity target acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it; a zero MaxForce leaves it active (measured). Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.F.documentation: Magnitude (the default) holds the force's length to MaxForce; PerAxis holds each axis of RelativeTo's frame to its lane of MaxAxesForce in Vector mode, each tangent axis to its lane of MaxPlanarAxesForce in Plane mode (a line keeps MaxForce).
Whether the force is limited (by ForceLimitMode); off, the target is reached within the step whatever it takes. Default true.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.L.documentation: The line Line mode holds the velocity along, in RelativeTo's frame (its length ignored; the zero vector holds nothing). Default (1, 0, 0).
The speed held along LineDirection in Line mode, studs per second. Default 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.M.documentation: The most force along each axis of RelativeTo's frame under the PerAxis limit in Vector mode; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (1000, 1000, 1000).

The most force, the assembly's weight included, under the Magnitude limit (and along a line under either), while ForceLimitsEnabled: the acceleration is MaxForce / mass until the target is reached (measured). Default 1000.
The most force along each tangent axis under the PerAxis limit in Plane mode; a lane of math.huge is no limit. Default (1000, 1000).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.P.documentation: The velocity held along the two tangent axes in Plane mode, studs per second. Default (0, 0).
Plane mode's first axis, in RelativeTo's frame. Default (1, 0, 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.R.documentation: Whether Attachment1's assembly takes the opposite force under RelativeTo Attachment1, the pair then sharing its momentum (an equal pair, one moving 3, ends at 1.5 each — measured). Default true.

The frame the target velocity, the line, the plane and the per-axis limits are named in: the world's (the default), Attachment0's, or Attachment1's — the velocity then relative to Attachment1's assembly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.S.documentation: Plane mode's second axis, in RelativeTo's frame, made perpendicular to the first. Default (0, 1, 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LinearVelocity.V.documentation: The velocity held in Vector mode, studs per second, in RelativeTo's frame: reached within a step while the force limit allows (measured). Default (0, 0, 0).
What the target holds: Vector (the default) the whole velocity, Line its component along LineDirection, Plane its projection on the two tangent axes.
Draws the editor's marker for the velocity target whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LocalScript.documentation: A script that runs on each client. Its CLASS decides that — a stored RunContext value is accepted but inert.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/LuaSourceContain.documentation: Anything that holds Luau source: the scripts and modules.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.documentation: A part whose geometry is an imported mesh. Size scales the mesh against its authored MeshSize; collision comes from the baked CollisionFidelity shapes; the mesh reference itself is immutable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.MeshId.documentation: The mesh asset reference, as the asset's local path — the empty string on a meshless husk. Every write is refused: the mesh reference is immutable after authoring.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MeshPart.MeshSiz.documentation: The authored mesh bounds, untouched by resizes. Every write is refused; resize through Size, which scales the mesh against these bounds.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/MessagingService.documentation: Topic messages within this server: SubscribeAsync connects a callback to a topic, PublishAsync sends a value to its subscribers, delivered on a later frame as one table { Data, Sent }. The engine runs one server per game, so a publish reaches no other server, and the reference's per-minute limits are not kept. The server's alone: a client side's call raises.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

Sends message to every subscriber of topic on this server: the value travels as JSON text (HttpService's codec, 1 KiB at most — `MessagingService:PublishAsync(): Cannot publish, data exceeded 1kb`) and arrives on a later frame as one table { Data, Sent }: a copy of the value and the session clock's Unix seconds at the publish (GetServerTimeNow's). A topic is 1 to 80 characters (`MessagingService: Topic names cannot be empty.`, `MessagingService: Topic names cannot be more than 80 characters.`). One server only: no other server receives it. The server's alone — a client side's call raises `MessagingService can only be executed by game server`.

Calls callback with every message published to topic on this server from now on — a table { Data, Sent } of its own per publish, the newest subscriber first, on a frame after it — and answers the connection: Disconnect stops the deliveries, and the script's end takes them with it. The topic is refused as PublishAsync's (empty, past 80 characters). The server's alone — a client side's call raises `MessagingService can only be executed by game server`.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.documentation: A grouping node for parts: pivots through PrimaryPart (or its bounding-box center without one) and moves as a group via PivotTo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.GetBoundin.documentation: The axis-aligned box around the subtree's parts, as (center CFrame, size). Errors when the subtree holds no part.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.GetPrimary.documentation: Deprecated: the PrimaryPart's CFrame. Errors when the model has no PrimaryPart or it no longer exists. Use GetPivot.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.PrimaryPar.documentation: The part the model pivots through, or nil. GetPivot and PivotTo use it; without one they fall back to the bounding-box center. A reference to a despawned part reads as nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Model.SetPrimary.documentation: Deprecated: moves the model by one rigid transform so its PrimaryPart lands at cframe — PivotTo through the PrimaryPart. Errors when the model has no PrimaryPart or it no longer exists. Use PivotTo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ModuleScript.documentation: Reusable code loaded with require: runs once per context, and its return value is cached and shared between requirers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberRange.documentation: An immutable min..max pair — the constructor refuses an inverted range. The particle ranges (Lifetime, Speed, Rotation, RotSpeed, FlipbookFramerate) speak it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequence.documentation: A piecewise-linear curve over a unit time span, built from 2 to 20 keypoints (the first at time 0, the last at time 1, in time order) — the particle curves Size, Squash and Transparency. Each keypoint's Envelope is a random half-width every particle samples its own offset within.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequence.K.documentation: The keypoints in time order — a fresh table on every read, as the reference hands out.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberSequenceKe.documentation: One NumberSequence keypoint: Time, Value and the random Envelope.
The half-width of the random band around the value (each particle picks its own offset within it).
The keypoint's position along the sequence, 0..1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/NumberValue.documentation: A named container for one double-precision number.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ObjectValue.documentation: A named container for one instance reference; references survive Destroy and read back as husks.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ObjectValue.Valu.documentation: The stored instance reference, or nil. References outlive Destroy — a destroyed target reads as its husk; assigning nil clears the slot.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/OrderedDataStore.documentation: An ordered store's object (identity OrderedDataStore < GlobalDataStore): whole numbers under keys, read one value at a time or as pages sorted by value — no key info, user ids or metadata.
The key's number — ONE value, no key info (measured); nothing for a key never written or removed. Yields while the store answers.

The live entries as { key, value } tables sorted by value — ascending or descending, ties by key — pageSize to a page (1 to 100, 50 by default, a numeric string taken as its number; else `106: PageSize must be within a predefined range`), between minValue and maxValue inclusive (measured); a non-numeric string raises `Unable to cast string to int` (the engine's). ascending is a boolean: a string raises `Unable to cast string to bool` (measured), nil `Argument 1 missing or nil` (the engine's). Yields while the store answers.
Adds delta (1 by default, rounded half away from zero) to the key's number — an absent key counts from 0 — and answers the new number (measured: 3 then 4). Yields while the store answers.
Removes the key and answers the number it held — nothing for a key with none. Yields while the store answers.

Writes a whole number (-2 and 2^53 measured; up to 2^63) and answers nothing; a fraction raises `103: double is not allowed in data stores.`, a string `103: string is not allowed in data stores.`, a boolean `103: bool is not allowed in data stores.` (measured). No user ids and no metadata on an ordered store. Yields while the store answers.

Calls transform with the key's number (nil for a key with none; no key info) and stores the whole number it returns, answering it (measured: 4 then 5); nil writes nothing. A transform that yields or errors is logged and the call answers nothing, as a DataStore's. Yields while the store answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.documentation: The positioned layer: everything with a pivot — parts and models — answers GetPivot and moves as a group through PivotTo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.GetPi.documentation: The instance's pivot: a Model's PrimaryPart pose (or its bounding-box center without one), an ordinary part's own CFrame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PVInstance.Pivot.documentation: Moves this instance and its logical descendants by ONE rigid transform: the subtree lands with its pivot at the target CFrame, members orbiting the pivot and rotating with it. A plain vector keeps the current rotation. Fires the pose signals for each moved object. A PrimaryPart-less Model pivots about its bounding-box center with identity rotation, so repeated ROTATING pivots compound there — a recorded divergence; give the model a PrimaryPart.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Part.documentation: The basic building block: a shaped, colored, physically simulated solid. Shape picks the geometry; the mesh and collider re-derive.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Part.Shape.documentation: The part's geometric shape. Writes accept the Enum.PartType item or its string name; the mesh and collider re-derive.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ParticleEmitter.documentation: A particle emitter under a part or an attachment: the flat property set (Rate, Lifetime, Speed, the Size/Transparency/Color sequences, the shape and flipbook enums, …) describes the effect, and each client's particle system realizes it — a headless server holds the description only. Emit, Clear and FastForward are local to the calling context. Enabled, Brightness, Color, Transparency, Shape, Size, Rotation and Orientation are the names it shares with other classes, each with its own particle-typed meaning here (docs/particle-system.md).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ParticleEmitter..documentation: A constant acceleration applied to every particle, in studs per second squared (gravity is not applied on its own).
A multiplier on the particle color (1 is unchanged; stored as written).
Removes every live particle of this emitter now.
The particle color over its lifetime, as a ColorSequence (a Color3 is refused — wrap it in ColorSequence.new).
Velocity damping per second (0 is none); stored as written.
The face of the parent part particles leave from. Writes accept the Enum.NormalId item or its name.
Spawns particleCount particles at once (default 16), Enabled or not — local to the calling context, never replicated. A negative count is a no-op; a string refuses.
`particleCount: number?`
Whether the emitter spawns at its Rate. Live particles finish their lives either way; Emit works while disabled.
Advances the emitter as if seconds had already passed — the steady state without the warm-up. Public here (an engine extension); zero or negative is a no-op.
`seconds: number`
Frames per second of the flipbook, picked uniformly within the range per particle.
The sprite grid the Texture holds: None, Grid2x2, Grid4x4 or Grid8x8 (Custom is refused — the engine has no custom grids).
How the grid plays over a particle's life: Loop, OneShot, PingPong or Random.
Whether each particle starts the flipbook on a random frame.
Each particle's life in seconds, picked uniformly within the range.
The blend from normal (0) to additive (1) — glowing particles lighten what is behind them; stored as written.
How much the scene's lighting affects the particles (0 unlit, 1 lit like a surface); stored as written.
Whether particles move with the parent after spawning (local space) instead of staying where they were born (world space).
How the particle quad faces: the camera, the camera about the world up, or along/across its velocity (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).
Particles spawned per second while Enabled. Stored as written (the reference accepts any number); a negative rate spawns nothing.
The spin in degrees per second, picked uniformly within the range.
The initial spin angle in degrees, picked uniformly within the range (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).
The emission volume: Box, Sphere, Cylinder or Disc. Writes accept the Enum.ParticleEmitterShape item or its name.
Which way particles leave the Shape: Outward, Inward or both.
How much of the Shape emits (1 is all of it); stored as written.
Whether particles spawn throughout the Shape (Volume) or on its boundary (Surface).
The particle size in studs over its lifetime, as a NumberSequence (the emitter branch of the dual-typed name).
The initial speed in studs per second, picked uniformly within the range.
The emission cone half-angles in degrees, per axis, around the EmissionDirection.
The particle's stretch over its lifetime: positive squashes along the velocity, negative stretches (0 is round).
The particle image, as a local asset path; the empty string is the engine's built-in soft disc. Strictly a string.
A multiplier on this emitter's clock (1 is real time), floored at 0 — the one particle property the reference clamps.
The particle transparency over its lifetime, as a NumberSequence (0 opaque, 1 invisible).
How much of the parent's velocity a new particle inherits (0 none, 1 all).
A render offset toward the camera in studs (positive is closer) — the ordering knob, since particles are not depth-sorted.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.documentation: A joined player's roster identity: UserId, the current Character (a dead one included until its respawn) with the CharacterAdded and CharacterRemoving signals, LoadCharacter, and the per-player RespawnTime (an engine extension — the reference engine keeps it on the Players service). Engine-spawned only; scripts reach players through the Players service.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.Character.documentation: The player's current character body — a dead one included, until the respawn replaces it — or nil while none is loaded (before the first spawn, with CharacterAutoLoads off, or once the player is leaving). CharacterAdded fires with each new one, CharacterRemoving with each one leaving.
Fires with the new character on every spawn, the first included.

Fires with the character just taken out of the world — the dead body a respawn replaces, the one LoadCharacter replaces, or a leaving player's. Delivered after the swap (measured): the old body's Parent is already nil and Character already the next body (nil on a leave), the old instance still readable; CharacterAdded follows in the same frame. The engine destroys the old body a frame later.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.DisplayNa.documentation: The player's Name (measured: Studio's test players and the signed-in account alike, a player that has left too). A script's write is refused with the reference's text, on the server and the client alike (measured): `The current thread cannot set 'Player's display name' (lacking capability WritePlayer)`.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.GetCamera.documentation: The player's camera state under server authority: CFrame, FieldOfView and ViewportSize. The CFrame rides the player's input stream, synchronized with the inputs of the same simulation tick (the server reads the camera the player's tick was played under — aim and look-direction logic); the other two replicate as properties do, at their own cadence. The server answers it for any player, a client only for its LocalPlayer; raises under the classic networking model.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.GetMouse.documentation: The player's mouse — the legacy cursor object (X/Y, UnitRay, Hit, Target, TargetFilter, Icon, the button and Move signals) built from the current camera and the local cursor. One object per player, the same on every call; a player that is not this process's reads the defaults and hears no signal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.GetNetwor.documentation: One-way network latency to this player's machine in seconds (half the measured round trip). The server answers it for any connected player; a client only for its LocalPlayer — a remote player reads -1 (measured: the reference's no-measurement sentinel), and any player in solo play reads 0 (no transport). Sampled, not instantaneous: it averages the transport's last five probes (one every ~5 s) off frame-boundary clock reads, so it floors near a frame's latency on a local link and trails a link that has just degraded.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.Kick.documentation: Removes the player from the game with an optional message (a number is taken as its text). The server may kick any player: its client's console prints `Server Kick Message: <message>; Metadata: `, its session ends and its world stays as it stood, and PlayerRemoving fires wherever the player is still held. A client may kick its LocalPlayer alone — another raises 'Cannot kick a non-local Player from a LocalScript' — which ends its session. In solo play the player leaves and no other joins for the rest of the run.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.LoadChara.documentation: Deprecated: the former name of LoadCharacterAsync, answered the same way — use LoadCharacterAsync.

Replaces the player's current character (dead or alive) with a fresh one, suspending the calling thread until the swap has landed: CharacterRemoving fires with the old one, CharacterAdded with the new one, and Character is the new one on return. The manual route when CharacterAutoLoads is off; the server's alone. Never returns in a place without a PlayerPrefab to load from.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.PlayerGui.documentation: The player's per-player UI container, engine-spawned at join and despawned with the player. Resolved by class, so renaming it does not hide it. Contents are client-local in v1 — UI neither serializes nor replicates.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.RespawnTi.documentation: Seconds between this player's death and their respawn, floored at 0. An engine extension over the Players service's RespawnTime: joins seed it from the service value, and a per-player write wins until the next service-level write (which writes through to the whole roster).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Player.UserId.documentation: Who the player is beyond its connection — what a save is keyed by, as far as the server can tell. A joined player reads what the server's identity policy settles on: its join number (1, 2, 3 … per server process), a guest's negative id of that session alone, the id its client claims, or a fold of its name — one player holds an id at a time. Solo play's player is -1, Studio's own id for its first test player (measured). Below 2^53 in magnitude, so it survives Luau's number type.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerGui.documentation: A player's UI container, engine-spawned under each Player at join. ScreenGuis parented here render for the LOCAL player only; contents are client-local (never saved, never replicated in v1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.documentation: The legacy cursor object Player:GetMouse returns (identity PlayerMouse < Mouse): the cursor in viewport pixels, the camera ray through it, the part and point it hits, a filter the cast ignores, an icon string, and the button, Move and Idle signals. Built from the current camera, the local cursor and the workspace cast; UserInputService is the modern surface.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Butt.documentation: Fires when the left mouse button goes down (this process's player only).
Fires when the left mouse button comes up.
Fires when the right mouse button goes down.
Fires when the right mouse button comes up.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Clas.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Dest.documentation: A no-op (measured): the mouse outlives the call and the next GetMouse answers the same object.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Hit.documentation: A CFrame at the point the cursor's ray hits, with Origin's rotation; 10000 studs from Origin when nothing is hit (measured). TargetFilter's subtree and the player's own character are ignored.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Icon.documentation: The cursor image's content id, stored as written; the empty string (the default) is the platform arrow. Nothing here draws it yet.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Idle.documentation: Fires on every frame no other mouse signal fired — not a stillness test, it fires between Move deliveries too.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.KeyD.documentation: Deprecated: the reference's retired key-down signal (measured to exist); never fires here — keys ride UserInputService.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.KeyU.documentation: Deprecated: the reference's retired key-up signal (measured to exist); never fires here — keys ride UserInputService.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Move.documentation: Fires on every frame the cursor's position changed.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Orig.documentation: A CFrame at UnitRay's origin — the current camera's near plane, measured — looking along it (the camera's roll ignored); the identity without a camera.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Targ.documentation: The part the cursor's ray hits, or nil (the sky, or nothing within 10000 studs).

An instance the cursor's cast ignores along with its descendants (nil, the default, ignores nothing beyond the player's own character). Only an Instance or nil can be assigned: `Unable to assign property TargetFilter. Instance expected, got number` (measured).
The face of Target the ray hits, as its NormalId; Right when nothing is hit (documented) — check Target first.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Unit.documentation: The unit ray through the cursor, its origin on the current camera's near plane — what Camera:ViewportPointToRay(X, Y) answers (measured); a zero ray without a camera.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.View.documentation: The current camera's viewport width in pixels (0 without a camera).
The current camera's viewport height in pixels (0 without a camera).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Whee.documentation: The reference's wheel-backward signal (measured to exist); never fires here.
The reference's wheel-forward signal (measured to exist); the engine's cursor carries no wheel, so it never fires.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.X.documentation: The cursor's horizontal position in viewport pixels from the left (0 without a cursor, and always for a player that is not this process's). Fires no property signal — connect Move.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerMouse.Y.documentation: The cursor's vertical position in viewport pixels from the top (0 without a cursor).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.documentation: The character template: joining players spawn their characters from it, SpawnCharacter builds NPCs from it, and its pose is where they stand.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Ass.documentation: The prefab body's angular velocity (zero without a live body).
The prefab body's center of mass in world space.
The prefab body's linear velocity (zero without a live body).
The prefab body's mass (zero without a live body).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.CFr.documentation: The prefab's full rigid transform as one CFrame value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Cen.documentation: The prefab body's local center of mass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Mas.documentation: The prefab body's mass (zero without a live body).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Pos.documentation: The prefab's world position — where characters spawned from it stand.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Rot.documentation: Deprecated: the prefab body's angular velocity — use AssemblyAngularVelocity.
The prefab's orientation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Spa.documentation: Spawns an unowned (NPC) character from this template and returns it, placed at position or standing on the prefab's own pose. Its Humanoid child answers the humanoid surface (Health, MoveTo, ...).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Tou.documentation: Fires when a collider starts touching the prefab body, with the other object.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PlayerPrefab.Vel.documentation: Deprecated: the prefab body's linear velocity — use AssemblyLinearVelocity.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.documentation: The session roster: LocalPlayer, the player list, join/leave signals, and the measured RespawnTime service property (consulted at death; each Player's per-player value seeds from it).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.Characte.documentation: Whether characters spawn automatically on join and after death (default true). When false only Player:LoadCharacter spawns one, and a dead body stays in the world until then. Consulted as joins and deaths happen — set it at boot.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.ClassNam.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.GetPlaye.documentation: The player with that UserId, or nil when nobody in the session has it — a fractional number is nobody's (measured); a numeric string converts. nil errors `Argument 1 missing or nil`; a non-number `Unable to cast <type> to User`.

The player whose Character is the given instance, or nil when it is nobody's (a dead body still counts until its respawn replaces it); nil answers nil (measured). A non-Instance errors `Unable to cast value to Object`.
Every player currently in the session, in unspecified order. A leaving player is already gone from it when its PlayerRemoving is delivered (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.LocalPla.documentation: This process's own player — nil until they join, and always nil on a dedicated server.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.PlayerAd.documentation: Fires with each player that joins the session — solo play's auto-created local player included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.PlayerRe.documentation: Fires with each player about to leave, while they are still on the roster and resolvable.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.RespawnT.documentation: Seconds between death and respawn (measured default 3). Stored as given — negatives read back and respawn promptly — and consulted at death: a write reaches players already in the game. Each Player's RespawnTime seeds from it and may override it per player.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Players.playerFr.documentation: Deprecated: the retired spelling of GetPlayerFromCharacter, answered the same way — use GetPlayerFromCharacter.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/PointLight.documentation: A light radiating in every direction from its parent's position.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.documentation: A seeded pseudo-random generator — the reference engine's own stream (PCG32), so a seed draws the same numbers here as there: NextNumber, NextInteger, NextUnitVector, an in-place Shuffle and Clone; two generators are equal when their states are. Random.new() with no seed draws from the VM's generator, the one math.random uses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.Clone.documentation: A second generator at the same state: neither moves the other.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.NextInteg.documentation: An integer between the bounds, each truncated toward zero and the two sorted: one draw for a span of up to 2^32 - 2 values, two for a wider one (the measured forms); a bound outside the 64-bit range, an infinity or a NaN is -2^63.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.NextNumbe.documentation: A number in [0, 1) from two draws of the measured generator, or with both bounds lo*(1 - u) + hi*u over the bounds SORTED; one argument refuses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.NextUnitV.documentation: A unit vector from two draws in single precision: a longitude over the full turn and a height uniform on [-1, 1].

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Random.Shuffle.documentation: Permutes the array part of t in place — from the end, one draw per position, raw reads and writes — and returns nothing. A nil within #t refuses before any draw; a dictionary alone is an empty array; a frozen table refuses after the first draw.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.documentation: An immutable origin + direction pair, as the camera's ScreenPointToRay/ViewportPointToRay hand out. Its own methods treat it as a half-line: ClosestPoint clamps at the origin and runs unbounded ahead.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.ClosestPoint.documentation: The nearest point on the ray to point: the projection onto the direction, clamped at the origin and unbounded ahead (the direction's length is not a limit).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Direction.documentation: The direction vector, exactly as constructed — any length.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Distance.documentation: The distance from point to its ClosestPoint on the ray.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Origin.documentation: The point the ray starts from.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Ray.Unit.documentation: The same ray with its direction normalized to unit length.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.documentation: The filter bundle Workspace:Raycast takes: both filter generations — FilterType over FilterDescendantsInstances (AddToFilter appends to it), and the newer ExcludeInstances / IncludeInstances pair, nil until written — all applied to a cast, each entry with its descendants; RespectCanCollide; the IgnoreWater, BruteForceAllSlow and CollisionGroup the reference keeps, stored and read back; and the engine's own ServerTime, the server time a cast rewinds the streamed parts to. Mutable; equal by value over the old members; RaycastParams.new() is the defaults.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Ad.documentation: Appends an instance, or every instance of a table (nested tables too), to FilterDescendantsInstances — the old list, duplicates kept — and returns nothing; anything else is `Expected a table or Instance` (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Br.documentation: Stored and read back, false by default; the engine's cast has no slow path to force.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Co.documentation: Stored and read back, "Default" by default (a number written is its text, measured); parts carry no collision group here, so a cast ignores it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Ex.documentation: The newer exclusion list, nil until written and independent of FilterType's pair: a cast applies both — the listed instances and their descendants never hit, whatever IncludeInstances says. A table of instances or nil (the old list's texts for the rest); never shown by tostring and outside == (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Fi.documentation: The instances FilterType applies to, each with its logical descendants; AddToFilter appends here. A read is a fresh copy (writing into it changes nothing); a write takes a table of instances, nested tables flattened — `Invalid value type; expected a table` otherwise, `Invalid value type; table must only contain Instances and other tables` for a wrong entry. A destroyed instance stays listed while a script value names it, and filters nothing.

How FilterDescendantsInstances reads: Exclude (the default) hides the listed instances and their descendants, Include admits them alone. An enum item only — a name string, a number or another enum's item is `Invalid value for enum 'RaycastFilterType'` (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Ig.documentation: Stored and read back, false by default; the engine has no terrain water for a cast to ignore.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.In.documentation: The newer inclusion list, nil until written and independent of FilterType's pair: nil admits everything, an empty list nothing, a list its instances and their descendants alone — less what ExcludeInstances and the old pair take away. A table of instances or nil; never shown by tostring and outside == (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Re.documentation: Whether a cast skips parts with CanCollide false; false by default (a ray hits them). Any value writes by truthiness.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RaycastParams.Se.documentation: An engine extension, the server alone: a server time in Workspace:GetServerTimeNow's seconds — the one a client read from GetRenderedServerTime when it fired — at which the cast tests every streamed root at the pose the server held then, the rest of the world live. Nil (the default) casts live; a number or nil only, a non-finite one refuses at the cast, and a client's cast refuses it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.documentation: The cross-network signal: FireServer and FireClient/FireAllClients queue OnServerEvent and OnClientEvent on the far side, payloads deep-copied through the remote codec.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.Fire.documentation: Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on every connected client with these arguments.
Server-side only: queues OnClientEvent on the given player's client with these arguments.
Client-side only: queues OnServerEvent on the server with these arguments. Payloads cross the remote codec — a real deep copy, even solo.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.OnCl.documentation: Fires on a client when the server calls FireClient or FireAllClients, with the fired arguments. Client-side only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteEvent.OnSe.documentation: Fires on the server when a client calls FireServer: the listener receives the sending player, then the fired arguments. Server-side only — touching it on a client errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.documentation: The cross-network call: InvokeServer and InvokeClient suspend the calling thread until the far handler's reply crosses back.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.I.documentation: Server-side only: calls the given player's OnClientInvoke and suspends until the reply, the player's disconnect (fails fast), or the timeout.

Client-side only: calls the server's OnServerInvoke and suspends the calling thread until the reply arrives — or an engine timeout errors it (the reference engine blocks forever; a recorded divergence). A handler error re-raises here with its text intact.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RemoteFunction.O.documentation: The client-side handler InvokeClient calls: it receives the arguments and its returns cross back to the server. Assign a function or nil; client-side only.
The server-side handler InvokeServer calls: it receives the invoking player, then the arguments, and its returns cross back to the caller. Assign a function or nil; server-side only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ReplicatedStorag.documentation: The container whose contents replicate to every client: shared modules and the templates a script clones into the world, which neither draw nor simulate until parented into the Workspace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.documentation: A rigid rod: the two attachments held Length apart, both free to turn.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.Ac.documentation: Whether the rod acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored. Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.Cu.documentation: The distance between the attachments in studs, read off the bodies; 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it moves.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.Le.documentation: The separation the rod holds its attachments at, in studs, rigidly. The measured default is 5; negative writes clamp to 0, as the rope's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.Li.documentation: The cone's half angle at Attachment0 in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Stored and saved, but inert: the rod turns freely at both ends (a recorded divergence). Default 90.
The cone's half angle at Attachment1 in degrees, while LimitsEnabled. Stored and saved, but inert, as LimitAngle0. Default 90.
Whether the rod's angle at each attachment is held within LimitAngle0 and LimitAngle1. Stored and saved, but inert: the rod turns freely at both ends (a recorded divergence). Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RodConstraint.Th.documentation: The thickness of the rod's marker in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RopeConstraint.documentation: A slack-allowed distance cap: the bodies never separate beyond Length, and the rope never pushes.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RopeConstraint.L.documentation: The rope's maximum separation in studs — slack allowed, it never pushes. The measured default is 5; negative writes clamp to 0.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.documentation: The frame clock: Heartbeat fires once per scripts pass with the frame's delta time. The one service whose Name ("Run Service", measured) differs from its ClassName.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.BindT.documentation: Client only: runs callback every frame in the render step, before RenderStepped, in ascending priority (Enum.RenderPriority values; bind order among equals), with the frame's delta time. Binding a name again adds a second binding, each running at its own priority (measured) — unbind before rebinding. A binding ends with UnbindFromRenderStep or the script. Accepted and never run from the server side.

Runs callback inside the fixed simulation loop, once per step its frequency divides (Hz30 by default: every second 60 Hz step — the simulation tick; Hz60 every step, down to Hz1), ahead of that step's physics, on the server and the client alike, in ascending priority (2000 by default; bind order among equals). deltaTime is the frequency's period exactly (1/30 for Hz30). A write here is what the step simulates. The returned connection is the unbind; a binding also ends with its script.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Class.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.GetPr.documentation: What instance is to this end: Authoritative on the server, Predicted on a client that predicts it under server authority, None otherwise (the classic rules apply). Readable inside a BindToSimulation callback, so one bound module can run on both ends and skip what neither end simulates.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.GetRe.documentation: The session tick, fractional, this frame draws at (an engine extension, GetSessionTick's counterpart for what is on screen): what a script reads to draw something that is a function of the tick — a scrolling track, a conveyor's marks — where the things beside it are drawn. With no instance, this end's own simulation: the server's and solo play's world, a client's predicted instances and what its own scripts made. Under server authority a mover written at the tick is shown one tick behind and eased across it, so the answer is GetSessionTick() - 1 plus the frame's phase through the tick; it runs on whether or not such an instance exists, so what is drawn from it never jumps when one stops or is gone, and a tick the session's numbering catches up or holds on a poor link is spread over the frames after it, as the bodies are shown. With an instance, where that instance is drawn (a welded part through its assembly's root): one this end simulates answers as above; a followed one is drawn at its playback's position — the tick the server's own snapshots give it, behind the server's present by the link and the playback's depth, running on while it rests; one the server moves that this end plays nothing back of answers with the followed world's median. Under the classic model nothing is eased across ticks (this end's own simulation answers GetSessionTick()) and poses carry no tick (a followed instance answers from the numbering, within a tick). -1 on a client before its numbering aligned.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.GetSe.documentation: The simulation tick this end stands at, numbered as the session numbers it (an engine extension; the reference has no tick API): the server's own count on the server and in solo play, on a client the server tick its fixed loop is at — its lead ahead of the server included, so an input consumed at tick N is applied by the server at its tick N. Inside a BindToSimulation callback the tick being simulated. -1 on a client before its numbering aligned. A game stamps its own remotes with it, so the other end knows the tick an action happened on.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Heart.documentation: Fires once per frame after the physics step with the frame's delta time in script-clock seconds. The workhorse per-frame hook; a write here renders this frame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsCli.documentation: True when this call runs on the client side: a connected client, or a LocalScript / RunContext Client script in solo play. A call with no script behind it answers false in solo, since an unattributed call is read as the server's. Exclusive with IsServer — no context answers both true.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsEdi.documentation: True in the editor with no game loaded; false while one runs, paused or not. The inverse of IsRunning except while paused, when both answer false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsRes.documentation: True while a BindToSimulation callback runs as part of a rollback's re-simulation rather than the step's first run; false otherwise.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsRun.documentation: True while the editor's Run is live, paused or not: the server side simulating alone, with no Player and no client. False in Play, Play Here, a multiplayer session, a standalone runtime and the editor's Idle.
True while a game is live and unpaused; false in the editor's Idle and while the simulation is paused. The inverse of IsEdit except while paused, when both answer false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsSer.documentation: True when this call runs on the server side: a dedicated server, or a server-kind script (legacy or RunContext Server) in solo play. A call with no script behind it — the command bar, a host-side call — answers true as well. Exclusive with IsClient — no context answers both true.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.IsStu.documentation: True in the editor and in the server/client processes its multiplayer session runner launches; false in a standalone runtime. The test-only-code guard.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Mispr.documentation: Client only: fires after a received authoritative state differed from the predicted one and the simulation was rolled back and re-run — with the fixed clock's seconds at the tick that diverged, the instances that did (each with the mismatched properties and attributes as { Predicted, Authoritative }, captured at that tick) and the stats ({ ResimulationTime } in seconds). Meant for debugging; a server-side connection never fires.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.PostS.documentation: Fires with Heartbeat, after the physics step, carrying the simulation's fixed step in seconds (Heartbeat carries the frame's real delta) — the reference's modern name for the same point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.PreAn.documentation: Fires first in the frame, just before Stepped, with the simulation's fixed step in seconds. The engine has no animation pass between the two yet; the hook exists so the reference's per-frame order holds.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.PreRe.documentation: The reference's modern name for RenderStepped: fires at the same point with the same delta, as its own signal (PreRender ~= RenderStepped). A server-side connection is accepted and never fires.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.PreSi.documentation: Fires with Stepped, before the physics step, carrying the simulation's fixed step in seconds — the reference's modern name for the same point.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Rende.documentation: Client only: fires every frame after Heartbeat and after the BindToRenderStep bindings, just before the frame renders, with the frame's delta time. A camera written here is what this frame shows. Connecting from the server side errors: "RenderStepped event can only be used from local scripts".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Rollb.documentation: Fires when the simulation rolls back to an earlier tick, before that tick and the ones since are re-simulated, with the fixed clock's seconds at the tick's start. Discard custom state kept past that time here; attributes of simulated instances are restored by the engine.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.SetCo.documentation: Client only, an engine extension: whether a correction of this predicted instance is shown spread over the engine's smoothing (the reference's SmoothDamp over 0.07 s, on by default) or as the raw one-frame snap. The smoothing is render-only — the instance's CFrame is corrected whole either way. Errors on the server ("SetCorrectionSmoothing can only be called on the client").

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.SetPr.documentation: Client only: forces prediction of instance On or Off, or hands it back to the engine (Automatic — v1 predicts the local character alone). Under server authority a predicted instance's pose, velocities and attributes are checked against every authoritative tick and a mismatch rolls back and re-simulates; under the classic model the mode is kept and nothing predicts. Errors on the server ("SetPredictionMode can only be called on the client") and inside a BindToSimulation callback.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Stepp.documentation: Fires once per frame before the physics step with (time, step): the seconds since the run started and the simulation's fixed step. A pose or force written here is what this frame simulates.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/RunService.Unbin.documentation: Removes every binding under name; an unknown name is a silent no-op.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.documentation: The screen-space UI root: its element tree renders over the viewport while Enabled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Displa.documentation: Stacking among ScreenGuis: higher draws on top; equal orders stack by creation.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Enable.documentation: Whether the ScreenGui's whole tree renders and receives input (true by default). Elements keep their state while disabled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ScreenGui.Ignore.documentation: Extends the tree under the reference engine's top inset. A recorded no-op here: the engine draws no inset, so the value stores and changes nothing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Script.documentation: A server-side script by default; RunContext can re-home it. Enabled is its run switch — disabling kills its threads, re-enabling restarts it fresh.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ServerScriptServ.documentation: The server's script container: its Scripts run on the server, and nothing in it replicates to a client.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ServerStorage.documentation: The server's own container: its contents never replicate to a client, and neither draw nor simulate until parented into the Workspace.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.documentation: A playable audio source: Play and Stop drive it, IsPlaying reads back, and volume, speed and looping are properties.
