@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.DidLoop.documentation: Fires per looped wrap with the SoundId and the loop count since Play — the engine clock's estimate, once the clip duration is known from the audio container's header.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Ended.documentation: Fires with the SoundId when a non-looped sound reaches its natural end (never on Stop). Playback ends where audio plays: on a dedicated server this signal never fires.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.IsPaused.documentation: The measured pause latch: set by Pause (even on a stopped sound), cleared by Play and Resume, untouched by Stop.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.IsPlaying.documentation: Whether the sound is audibly playing — Play/Stop/Pause/Resume drive it, a finished non-looped sound writes it back to false, and a paused sound reads false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Loaded.documentation: Fires with the SoundId when the audio asset finishes loading. Assets load where audio plays: on a dedicated server this signal never fires.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.LoopRegion.documentation: The span a looped sound loops inside while PlaybackRegionsEnabled — play through once, then wrap from its max back to its min (the intro-then-loop music shape).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Looped.documentation: Whether playback restarts from the top when the clip ends.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Pause.documentation: Freezes playback in place: IsPlaying reads false, TimePosition holds, and the latch shows in IsPaused. Play restarts from the top; Resume continues from here. The measured contract.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Paused.documentation: Fires with the SoundId when the pause latch engages.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Play.documentation: Starts playback (IsPlaying becomes true) — from a still-pending explicit TimePosition write (the authored value included), otherwise from 0. Calling Play on a playing sound restarts it from the top. The measured reference contract.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.PlaybackRe.documentation: The playable span in seconds while PlaybackRegionsEnabled: playback starts at its min and a one-shot ends at its max (the measured fresh range is 0..60000).
Whether the playback regions apply: playback then starts at PlaybackRegion's min, a one-shot ends at its max, and a looped sound loops inside LoopRegion.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.PlaybackSp.documentation: Playback rate (1 is normal speed), clamped to 0..20 — the measured reference range. Pitch follows the rate.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Played.documentation: Fires with the SoundId on every acted Play — restarts included, and remotely applied plays too.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Resume.documentation: Plays from the CURRENT TimePosition with no rewind — a paused sound continues, and (measured) even a stopped sound starts where it stands.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Resumed.documentation: Fires with the SoundId when the latch releases into playback (Resume; a fresh Play fires Played instead).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.RollOffMax.documentation: Positional playback is silent at and beyond this distance in studs (floored at 0), whatever the roll-off mode.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.RollOffMin.documentation: Positional playback holds full volume within this distance in studs (floored at 0); attenuation starts beyond it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.RollOffMod.documentation: The attenuation curve between RollOffMinDistance and RollOffMaxDistance: Inverse (the default), Linear, LinearSquare, or InverseTapered. Writes accept the Enum.RollOffMode item or its string name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.SoundGroup.documentation: The volume bus this sound plays through: a SoundGroup instance or nil. Assigning anything else errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.SoundId.documentation: The audio asset, as a local asset path.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Stop.documentation: Stops a playing sound and rewinds TimePosition to 0 (IsPlaying becomes false). On a sound that is not playing it is a no-op — a pending TimePosition write survives. The measured contract.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Stopped.documentation: Fires with the SoundId when Stop acts (a no-op Stop is silent; the natural end fires Ended instead).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.TimeLength.documentation: The clip length in seconds, 0 until the engine knows it — resolved from the audio container's header under the host's asset root (the reference also reads 0 before load).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.TimePositi.documentation: Playback position in seconds, stored as written (playback treats a negative as 0). Advances while the sound plays (an engine-side estimate); writing it seeks a playing sound, and a written position still pending when Play is called is where playback starts (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Sound.Volume.documentation: Playback volume, clamped to 0..10 (the measured reference range). The effective loudness multiplies in the assigned SoundGroup's Volume.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundGroup.documentation: A volume bus: every Sound whose SoundGroup points here plays at its own Volume multiplied by the group's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundGroup.Volum.documentation: The bus multiplier, clamped to 0..10 like Sound.Volume: every Sound in the group plays at its own Volume times this.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.documentation: Non-positional playback: PlayLocalSound starts a Sound wherever it lives, storage included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Cla.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Nam.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SoundService.Pla.documentation: Starts a Sound non-positionally, wherever it lives — storage included. Anything but a Sound instance errors.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpawnLocation.documentation: A Part players spawn on. Otherwise a regular part — every BasePart member applies.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpotLight.documentation: A cone light aimed along its parent's orientation; Angle is the full cone in degrees.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpotLight.Angle.documentation: The full cone angle in degrees, clamped 0..180 (writing 200 reads back 180). A default spot light reads 90.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/SpringConstraint.documentation: A spring between the two attachments: it pulls them toward FreeLength with Stiffness force per stud of stretch (measured: k·x = m·g), slowed by Damping, within MinLength and MaxLength while LimitsEnabled.

Whether the spring acts: Enabled, in the workspace, both attachments on parts in the workspace, two assemblies, one of them not anchored (an anchored end leaves it active, as a hinge's anchored axle — measured). Read only.
The number of coils the spring's marker draws: cosmetic. Default 3.
The distance between the attachments in studs, read off the bodies; 0 while either end is on no body. Read only; it fires no Changed as it moves.

How quickly the spring's oscillation dies down: a force of Damping per stud a second of the attachments' relative speed. 0 (the default) oscillates on; on the measured hung cube 60 settles and 5 still swings after 6 seconds.
The length the spring rests at, in studs: further apart it pulls, closer it pushes. Default 1.
Whether the spring's length stops hard at MinLength and MaxLength, without a bounce. Default false.
The most force the spring applies. Stored and saved, but inert: the spring's force is never capped (a recorded divergence). Default inf.
The most separation the spring allows while LimitsEnabled, in studs. Default 5.
The least separation the spring allows while LimitsEnabled, in studs. Default 0.
The radius of the spring marker's coils in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.4.

The spring's force per stud of stretch past FreeLength (or of compression short of it): a 5.6-mass cube hung on Stiffness 100 rests about 11 studs past FreeLength, k·x = m·g (the reference 10.979, the engine 10.960 where the cube falls asleep — measured). The default 0, anything less, or a stiffness below 1e-30 pulls nothing.
The thickness of the spring marker's wire in studs: cosmetic. Default 0.1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.documentation: The switch on the engine's built-in interfaces: SetCoreGuiEnabled shows or hides the player list (Enum.CoreGuiType.PlayerList, the one drawn today) or every kind at once, GetCoreGuiEnabled reads the store. The container of authored ScreenGuis the reference's service also is waits on UI serialization.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.Class.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.GetCo.documentation: Whether a built-in interface is shown — true until SetCoreGuiEnabled says otherwise; `All` reads true only when every kind is (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterGui.SetCo.documentation: Shows or hides one of the engine's built-in interfaces on this client: `Enum.CoreGuiType.PlayerList` is the player list (the one drawn today), `All` every kind at once; the other kinds are remembered for GetCoreGuiEnabled. The item, its name or its value; the flag cast the reflection's way (a number by zero/nonzero, "true"/"false"). A server accepts and stores the call without drawing anything (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StarterPlayerScr.documentation: The client scripts' container, directly under `game` here (the reference's sits under StarterPlayer): its contents replicate, and its LocalScripts run on each client.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/StringValue.documentation: A named container for one string.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.documentation: Typed text input: click (or CaptureFocus) to focus, keystrokes edit Text, Enter or clicking away releases — FocusLost says which. ClearTextOnFocus, TextEditable and MultiLine behave like the reference engine; no cursor or selection yet (v1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.CaptureF.documentation: Gives this box keyboard focus, releasing any other focused box (its FocusLost fires with false).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.ClearTex.documentation: Empties Text when the box gains focus (true by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.FocusLos.documentation: Fires when the box loses focus, with enterPressed: true for Return, false for Escape, a click elsewhere, or ReleaseFocus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.Focused.documentation: Fires (with no arguments) when the box gains keyboard focus — a click or CaptureFocus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.Font.documentation: The typed text's legacy typeface enum over FontFace (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.FontFace.documentation: The typed text's typeface as a Font value (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.IsFocuse.documentation: Whether this box holds keyboard focus right now.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.MultiLin.documentation: Return inserts a newline instead of releasing focus.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.ReleaseF.documentation: Releases this box's focus; FocusLost fires with the submitted flag (false when omitted). A no-op while unfocused.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.RichText.documentation: Renders the typed Text as rich-text markup (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.Text.documentation: The typed content. Keystrokes edit it while the box holds focus; writes land like any property.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextEdit.documentation: Whether keystrokes edit Text. A non-editable box still focuses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextScal.documentation: Scales the typed text to fill the box (capped at 100 px).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextSize.documentation: The typed text's size in pixels, clamped to 1..100.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextStro.documentation: The typed text's outline color (see TextLabel).
The typed text outline's transparency (1 by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextXAli.documentation: How the typed lines sit horizontally (Center by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextBox.TextYAli.documentation: Where the typed text block sits vertically (Center by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.documentation: A clickable UI element with a text label; Activated fires on click release.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.Font.documentation: The label's legacy typeface enum over FontFace (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.FontF.documentation: The label's typeface as a Font value (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.RichT.documentation: Renders the label's Text as rich-text markup (see TextLabel).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.Text.documentation: The button's label text. Same-value writes are silent.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextS.documentation: Scales the label's text to fill the button (capped at 100 px); TextSize is ignored while set.
The button label's text size in pixels, clamped to 1..100.
The label outline's transparency (1, invisible, by default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextX.documentation: How the label's lines sit horizontally: Left, Center (the default) or Right. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextButton.TextY.documentation: Where the label's text block sits vertically: Top, Center (the default) or Bottom. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.documentation: A UI element that displays text.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.Font.documentation: The legacy typeface enum beside FontFace: reads the item the last Font write stored — a fresh label reads Legacy, a face written through FontFace reads Unknown (measured), an authored face the item whose face it equals; a write of an item, its name or its value rewrites FontFace with the item's face and fires both signals. Unknown is silently ignored (measured).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.FontFa.documentation: The typeface as a Font value: Family is a local font asset path (.ttf/.otf; the empty string is the engine default face), Weight and Style the reference enums. Reads are copies; only a Font can be assigned.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.RichTe.documentation:
Renders Text as rich-text markup: `` `` `` ``, ``, `
` and the XML escapes. Malformed markup renders raw.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.Text.documentation: The displayed text ("Label" on a fresh instance, as measured). Same-value writes are silent — a HUD may rewrite its label every frame without re-triggering layout.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSc.documentation: Scales the rendered text to fill the element (capped at 100 px); TextSize is ignored while set.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSi.documentation: The text size in pixels, clamped to 1..100 (the reference range; 8 on a fresh instance, as measured; TextScaled ignores it).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextSt.documentation: The outline color behind the glyphs (black by default; invisible until TextStrokeTransparency drops below 1).
How see-through the outline renders, clamped 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible — the default).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextXA.documentation: How lines sit horizontally in the element: Left, Center (the default) or Right. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TextLabel.TextYA.documentation: Where the text block sits vertically in the element: Top, Center (the default) or Bottom. Writes accept the enum item or its name.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Torque.documentation: A mover: a constant torque on Attachment0's assembly every physics step, named in RelativeTo's frame.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Torque.Active.documentation: Whether the torque acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it. Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Torque.RelativeT.documentation: The frame Torque is named in: Attachment0's (the default), Attachment1's, or the world's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Torque.Torque.documentation: The torque applied to Attachment0's assembly every physics step, in RelativeTo's frame. Default (0, 0, 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Torque.Visible.documentation: Draws the editor's marker for the torque whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TriangleMeshPart.documentation: The mesh-geometry layer: how imported meshes turn into collision shapes (CollisionFidelity).

How the mesh's collision geometry is built: a Box, one convex Hull, or the decomposed convex shapes of Default and PreciseConvexDecomposition. Writes re-bake the collider — what the property says is what collides.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.documentation: One running property animation — the handle TweenService:Create returns (identity Tween < TweenBase, measured). Play, Pause and Cancel drive it; Completed fires the final Enum.PlaybackState.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Cancel.documentation: Stops the tween and leaves every property where it stands (the measured shape); Completed fires Cancelled.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.ClassName.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Completed.documentation: Fires once when the tween ends — Enum.PlaybackState.Completed on a natural finish, Cancelled after Cancel (or after a later tween claimed a shared property). The handle is spent afterwards.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Name.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Pause.documentation: Freezes a playing tween where it stands; Play resumes from there.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Tween.Play.documentation: Starts (or resumes after Pause) the tween: captures the current values as the from-side and runs on the script clock. A later Play on a shared property cancels the earlier tween.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.documentation: The parameter bundle TweenService:Create consumes: duration, easing style and direction, repeats, reversal and delay — immutable once built.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.DelayT.documentation: Seconds to wait before the tween starts playing.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Easing.documentation: Which end of the curve eases: In, Out, or InOut.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Repeat.documentation: How many extra times the tween repeats after the first play; 0 plays once.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenInfo.Revers.documentation: Whether the tween plays back to the start after each forward pass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.documentation: Property animation: Create builds a Tween driving properties to goal values through the reference engine's easing curves (pinned to its live samples); GetValue exposes the curves directly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Cla.documentation: The class name — the first name IsA answers.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Cre.documentation: Builds a Tween driving the given properties of one instance to their goal values (v1 tracks: Transparency, Color, Size, Position, Volume, WalkSpeed — each must exist on the target's class). The handle starts idle; Play starts it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Get.documentation: The eased interpolation alpha for a raw 0..1 alpha — the same curves the tweens themselves run on, pinned to the reference engine's samples.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.IsA.documentation: The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".

@bettervoxel/globaltype/TweenService.Nam.documentation: The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim.documentation: The one-axis UI coordinate: a parent-relative scale plus a pixel offset. The UI modifier instances (UICorner, UIPadding) speak it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim.Scale.documentation: The scale component: a fraction of the relevant parent dimension.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.documentation: The UI coordinate: a parent-relative scale plus a pixel offset per axis. GuiObject Position and Size speak it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.Height.documentation: The Y axis under its other name: the same UDim as Y.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.Lerp.documentation: Interpolates toward goal by alpha, unclamped (-0.5 and 1.5 extrapolate): the scales as floats, the offsets rounded to the nearest integer, a half away from zero (measured). A missing goal or alpha errors `Argument N missing or nil`, a wrong one `Unable to cast <type> to UDim2` / `to float`.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.Width.documentation: The X axis under its other name: the same UDim as X.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.X.documentation: The X axis as a UDim: the fraction of the parent's width plus the pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.Y.documentation: The Y axis as a UDim: the fraction of the parent's height plus the pixel offset.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UDim2.lerp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Lerp, answered the same way (measured) — use Lerp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIBase.documentation: The root of the UI modifier family; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIComponent.documentation: A modifier instance: parented under a GuiObject, it restyles that PARENT element and renders nothing itself.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UICorner.documentation: Rounds its parent element's corners by CornerRadius — a UDim: a fraction of the shorter side plus pixels.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UICorner.CornerR.documentation: How far the parent element's corners round: a fraction of the shorter side plus pixels. The measured default is (0, 8).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.documentation: Tints its parent element's fill with a color ramp: Color (a ColorSequence), Transparency (a NumberSequence) and Rotation in degrees (0 = left to right).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Color.documentation: The color ramp multiplied into the parent element's fill.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Rotat.documentation: The ramp's direction in degrees: 0 runs left to right, 90 top to bottom.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGradient.Trans.documentation: A transparency ramp multiplied into the fill's alpha.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIGridStyleLayou.documentation: The grid-style layout layer (list and grid layouts descend from it); no members of its own here.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UILayout.documentation: The layout-modifier layer of the UIComponent family; it adds no members of its own.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.documentation: Lays its parent's children out in a line: FillDirection, Padding between items, the alignment pair, and SortOrder (Name by default, or LayoutOrder). A laid-out child's Position and AnchorPoint are ignored.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Fil.documentation: The line's axis: Vertical (the default) or Horizontal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Hor.documentation: Where the line sits horizontally in the parent: Left (the default), Center or Right.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Sor.documentation: What orders the siblings: Name (the default, as measured) or LayoutOrder (Custom is the legacy alias).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIListLayout.Ver.documentation: Where the line sits vertically in the parent: Top (the default), Center or Bottom.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIPadding.documentation: Insets its parent element's content box per side (PaddingTop, PaddingBottom, PaddingLeft, PaddingRight — each a UDim).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIPadding.Paddin.documentation: The inset from the parent element's bottom edge.
The inset from the parent element's left edge.
The inset from the parent element's right edge.
The inset from the parent element's top edge.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.documentation: Outlines its parent element: Color, Thickness, Transparency and ApplyStrokeMode. v1 renders both modes as the box outline (the reference engine's Contextual strokes text on text elements).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.ApplySt.documentation: What the stroke outlines: Contextual (the default) or Border. v1 renders both as the box outline (the reference engine's Contextual strokes TEXT on text elements — recorded divergence; the TextStroke properties cover that need).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.Thickne.documentation: The outline width in pixels, floored at 0 (the default is 1).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UIStroke.Transpa.documentation: How see-through the outline renders, clamped 0 (opaque, the default) to 1 (invisible).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/UserInputService.documentation: The raw input layer: InputBegan/InputEnded with Enum.KeyCode/Enum.UserInputType payloads, IsKeyDown polling, and the mouse position and per-frame delta. The authored Keybinds layer reads the same input state; this is the Roblox-parity surface underneath it.
The class name — the first name IsA answers.
The TextBox currently holding keyboard focus, or nil. The guard for raw polling (IsKeyDown) while the player types; the InputBegan path already reports gameProcessed instead.
This frame's mouse motion as a Vector2 (dx, dy).
The cursor's logical position in the player window as a Vector2 — (0, 0) when no window exists.
Fires on every key or mouse-button press with a read-only input table and a gameProcessed flag (always false until UI focus exists). Mouse buttons carry KeyCode None.
InputBegan's release half: fires when the key or mouse button comes back up, with the same payload shape.
The ancestry test: true for the class name, any measured base (the DataModel is a ServiceProvider, a Tween is a TweenBase) and "Instance".
Whether the key is held right now. Accepts the enum item or its name; unknown or unmapped keys are simply not down.

How the cursor behaves while the game owns it (a Scriptable or any other non-orbit camera) and the player window has focus: Default leaves it free, LockCenter pins it to the window's center every frame, LockCurrentPosition where it is — a lock keeps GetMouseDelta flowing. Focus loss frees the cursor and focus restores the lock. Accepts the item or its name; an orbit camera's own rule (first person hides, the drag pins) stands regardless.
Whether the cursor is drawn while the game owns it and the window has focus (default true). Read as a raw boolean.
The display name: the class name again, except RunService (measured "Run Service") and the DataModel, whose Name is the place name ("Game" is the recorded stub until the engine carries one).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/ValueBase.documentation: The value-container family: one typed Value property plus a Changed signal that fires with the new value.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.documentation: An immutable 2D vector (a userdata, unlike Vector3): X/Y in both casings, Magnitude and Unit, the arithmetic operators against a Vector2 or a number (the operators are not listed below — they are metamethods, like CFrame's `*`), and the method set. SpreadAngle speaks it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Angle.documentation: The angle to other in radians: unsigned (0..π) by default, signed (-π..π, counter-clockwise positive) when isSigned is true.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Ceil.documentation: Each component rounded up to an integer.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Cross.documentation: The 2D cross product with other — a scalar, the signed area of the parallelogram the two vectors span.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Floor.documentation: Each component rounded down to an integer.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.FuzzyEq.documentation: Whether every component is within epsilon (default 1e-5) of other's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Lerp.documentation: The linear interpolation toward goal by alpha (0 = this vector, 1 = goal).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Sign.documentation: The sign of each component: -1, 0 or 1.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.Unit.documentation: The same direction at unit length (NaN components for the zero vector, the native vector's answer).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.lerp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Lerp, answered the same way (measured) — use Lerp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.magnitud.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Magnitude (the reference answers both) — use Magnitude.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.unit.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Unit (the reference answers both, measured) — use Unit.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.x.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of X (the reference answers both) — use X.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector2.y.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Y (the reference answers both) — use Y.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.documentation: Roblox's Vector3 IS Luau's native vector here — one type, two dialects: Vector3.new(1, 2, 3) equals vector.create(1, 2, 3), uppercase X/Y/Z/Magnitude/Unit and the method set ride a type metatable, and lowercase x/y/z stay on the VM fast path. Recorded divergence: typeof says 'vector'. The per-value member surface is not yet in the API model; the constructors below are.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Angle.documentation: The angle to other in radians: unsigned (0..π), or signed by the rotation's sense around axis when one is given.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Cross.documentation: The cross product with other: perpendicular to both, by the right-hand rule.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.FuzzyEq.documentation: Whether each component is within epsilon of other's (1e-5 when omitted).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Lerp.documentation: The point alpha of the way from this vector to goal.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Max.documentation: The componentwise maximum of this vector and the others.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Min.documentation: The componentwise minimum of this vector and the others.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.Unit.documentation: The vector scaled to length 1, in its own direction.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.lerp.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Lerp, answered the same way — use Lerp.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.magnitud.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Magnitude, answered the same way — use Magnitude.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.unit.documentation: Deprecated: the retired lowercase spelling of Unit, answered the same way — use Unit.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.x.documentation: The X component, the native vector's own lane: read with no metatable, the VM's fast path.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.y.documentation: The Y component, the native vector's own lane: read with no metatable, the VM's fast path.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Vector3.z.documentation: The Z component, the native vector's own lane: read with no metatable, the VM's fast path.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.documentation: A mover: a constant force on Attachment0's assembly every physics step, named in RelativeTo's frame, at Attachment0 (turning the assembly by its arm) or at the centre of mass.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.Acti.documentation: Whether the force acts: Enabled, in the workspace, Attachment0 on a part that is not anchored, and Attachment1 on a body when RelativeTo names it; a zero Force leaves it active (measured). Read only.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.Appl.documentation: Whether the force acts at the assembly's centre of mass (no turn) instead of at Attachment0. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.Forc.documentation: The force pushed on Attachment0's assembly every physics step, in RelativeTo's frame; off the centre of mass it turns the assembly too (measured). Default (1000, 0, 0).

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.Rela.documentation: The frame Force is named in: Attachment0's (the default — it turns with the assembly), Attachment1's, or the world's.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/VectorForce.Visi.documentation: Draws the editor's marker for the force whatever the selection. An authoring aid — nothing at runtime reads it. Default false.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Weld.documentation: A classic joint: while Active, Part0.CFrame * C0 equals Part1.CFrame * C1, and the part that is not the assembly root stands where the frames put it — creating the weld, or writing C0, C1, an end or Enabled, moves it. Inactive between two anchored parts.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.documentation: Rigidly binds Part0 to Part1: while Enabled the two parts move as one assembly.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.E.documentation: Whether the weld holds. Disabling releases the bond without deleting the constraint; re-enabling re-welds at the parts' current poses.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WeldConstraint.P.documentation: One end of the weld: an Instance or nil. When both ends are set and Enabled, the parts move as one rigid assembly.
The other end of the weld: an Instance or nil.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.documentation: The root every world object lives under — the `workspace` global. A real class with Model ancestry (measured): it answers PrimaryPart, GetPivot and GetBoundingBox like a Model, refuses the part pose surface, and carries the world-level members Gravity and Raycast.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Author.documentation: The place's networking model for this run: Server (the server simulates everything, clients send inputs, predict and roll back) or Automatic (the classic model, an owner per assembly). Authored in the place file's world section; read-only here as in the reference.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Curren.documentation: The camera the eye renders through — nil where there is none (a dedicated server). Assigning a Camera parented under the workspace makes it current and DETACHES the previous one (Parent nil, alive); an assignee parented elsewhere is replaced the next frame by a fresh Fixed camera, as is a destroyed current camera (measured). Fires its property signal on every change, the engine's included.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.GetRen.documentation: The server time, in GetServerTimeNow's seconds, the other players' parts are drawn at this frame on a client — the playback's position behind the server (an engine extension). With an instance, that part's own drawn instant, which differs from the world's by a few milliseconds: pass the part a shot hit on the client, so the server's cast (workspace:Raycast with params.ServerTime) finds it where it was drawn — half a stud matters on a fast ship. On the server, and for anything this client does not play back, the server time now.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.GetSer.documentation: The server's Unix time in seconds, as this end's session clock estimates it: the server's and solo play's own wall clock, a client's estimate of it — every end reads roughly the same value, whatever its own clock says. Monotonic, and moving at the local clock's rate; for a precise interval use os.clock. Raises on a client before it has joined a server.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Gravit.documentation: The global gravity magnitude in studs per second squared, applied downward. Parts and the character controller both read it.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/Workspace.Raycas.documentation: Casts a ray from origin along direction — the vector's length is the range. Returns a hit record (Instance, Position, Normal, Distance) or nil. The optional RaycastParams filters by both generations — FilterType over FilterDescendantsInstances, and ExcludeInstances / IncludeInstances — all applied, each entry with its descendants, RespectCanCollide skipping CanCollide-false parts; the engine also takes a plain table of the same keys (FilterType, FilterDescendantsInstances, RespectCanCollide, ServerTime). On the server under server authority, ServerTime (an engine extension: a server time in GetServerTimeNow's seconds — the one a client read from GetRenderedServerTime when it fired) tests every streamed part at the pose the server held at that time and the rest of the world live, so a shot aimed at what a client drew hits what it drew; a time older than the second the history keeps clamps to it. A client cannot pass it: it casts at the poses it draws. Validate the shot's origin against the shooter yourself, as the reference advises: the engine rewinds the targets, not the gun.

@bettervoxel/globaltype/WorldRoot.documentation: Workspace's measured parent in the class tree, between Model and the root — it carries no members of its own here.
